title: Applied Science Intern
description:
Job Description

Thomson Reuters Labs is seeking a curious and open-minded Applied Science Intern with a passion for machine learning and natural language processing. In this six-month internship, you'll join a diverse, interdisciplinary global team of specialists in Information Retrieval, NLP, Machine Learning, Engineering, and Design. You'll be part of Thomson Reuters' digital and AI transformation, contributing to real-world challenges and high-growth products across our core segments: Legal, Tax & Accounting, Government, and Reuters News.


We experiment, we build, we deliver. You'll experience the entire model development lifecycle—from ideation through testing and deployment—while learning from world-class researchers and engineers. This is an opportunity to contribute to applied research and development that drives innovation and serves Thomson Reuters customers in new and exciting ways.


Internship Details: 6-month duration with flexible start date aligned with your availability.


Key Responsibilities

  • Participate in the full model development lifecycle, including building, testing, and delivering high-quality machine learning and NLP solutions that address real-world business challenges.
  • Collaborate with a cross-functional global team of machine learning engineers, NLP specialists, data scientists, and product teams, learning from and partnering with colleagues across multiple time zones and disciplines.
  • Innovate by experimenting with new approaches, learning emerging technologies, and contributing original ideas to solve complex problems in information retrieval, natural language understanding, and machine learning applications.

Required Qualifications

  • Enrolled in or holding an MSc degree in Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Science, or a closely related discipline, or currently pursuing a PhD in a relevant field
  • Understanding and hands-on experience with Natural Language Processing and/or Machine Learning methods, including exposure to Large Language Models
  • Proficiency in Python and practical experience implementing solutions using deep learning, machine learning, and NLP frameworks and tools
  • Experience designing, creating, and evaluating experiments related to machine learning or large language models, with a data-driven problem-solving mindset
  • Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively as part of a diverse, distributed team

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with code collaboration and versioning systems such as GitHub
  • Familiarity with cloud platforms such as Amazon AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud
  • Experience working with unstructured datasets and knowledge of data cleaning, processing, and preparation techniques
  • Enthusiasm for staying current with state-of-the-art machine learning and NLP research and techniques
  • Curiosity, intellectual openness, and a genuine passion for problem-solving through applied AI and machine learning

#LI-CH1


What’s in it For You?

  • Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment (2-3 days a week in the office depending on the role) for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.

  • Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.

  • Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.

  • Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.

  • Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.

  • Social Impact: Make an impact in your community with our Social Impact Institute. We offer employees two paid volunteer days off annually and opportunities to get involved with pro-bono consulting projects and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives.

  • Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

About Us

Thomson Reuters informs the way forward by bringing together the trusted content and technology that people and organizations need to make the right decisions. We serve professionals across legal, tax, accounting, compliance, government, and media. Our products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. Reuters, part of Thomson Reuters, is a world leading provider of trusted journalism and news.

We are powered by the talents of 26,000 employees across more than 70 countries, where everyone has a chance to contribute and grow professionally in flexible work environments. title: Senior Buyer Chassis
description:
ABOUT SLATE

At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. The spirit of DIY and customization runs throughout every element of a Slate, because people should have control over how their trucks look, feel, and represent them.

| WHAT YOU GET TO DO


Category Sourcing & Strategy

Own and set the sourcing strategy for complex, high-value, or multiple commodity categories, building a resilient supply base that meets Slate’s cost, quality, delivery, and Job 1 launch targets. Lead RFIs, RFQs, and commercial negotiations for production parts, service parts, tooling, and services, and independently resolve cost, quality, and delivery issues as they arise.

Lead cross-functional sourcing strategy in partnership with Engineering, Quality, Program Management, Cost Estimating, and Finance to drive supplier readiness, supply chain risk mitigation, and launch timing. Serve as a category expert and trusted advisor to the broader Purchasing team while ensuring adherence to Slate Global Terms and Conditions.


Contract & Commercial Management

  • Independently negotiate complex, multi-million-dollar supply agreements, including pricing, payment terms, lead times, and quality specifications
  • Negotiate and administer long-term supply agreements, blanket orders, and consignment programs aligned with demand planning
  • Administer NDA processes and manage General Terms & Conditions (GTCs), Purchased Part Agreements (PPAs), and other supplier contracts throughout their lifecycle
  • Oversee change management and PO updates during design phases, and manage pricing adjustments for raw materials per contract terms

Supplier Relationship Management & Development

  • Develop and execute category strategies that align the supply base with Slate’s cost, quality, and capacity needs
  • Lead RFQ/RFP processes and competitive bid analysis, and prepare business cases to support sourcing decisions
  • Own strategic supplier relationships through regular business reviews and performance scorecards (OTD, quality, pricing, service)
  • Drive supplier development, qualification, and onboarding in partnership with Quality and Engineering teams
  • Lead escalation resolution for supply disruptions, quality escapes, and delivery issues to protect production continuity
  • Hold suppliers accountable to agreed performance, quality, and delivery commitments through corrective action plans

Commodity Strategy, Risk Management & Cost Savings

  • Be accountable for enterprise-level cost reduction targets across categories, identifying and delivering measurable year-over-year savings
  • Drive commodity strategy and risk mitigation, including forward contracting and index-linked pricing
  • Own full supply chain risk mapping and mitigation strategy for critical categories, including sub-tier visibility
  • Monitor commodity markets and price trends, and provide commodity forecasts and cost models to support annual budgeting
  • Serve as liaison between Purchasing and Cost Estimating to align material pricing with project estimates and review estimated vs. actual costs
  • Use spend analysis and reporting to identify savings opportunities and prepare period-end procurement reports

Leadership & Collaboration

  • Operate with full autonomy while keeping Procurement leadership informed on category performance, risks, and savings
  • Mentor Buyer I and Buyer II team members and informally lead category teams
  • Partner with Engineering, Quality, and Program teams to ensure early procurement involvement in new program launches

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TEAM

Education & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Engineering, or related field preferred
  • 10+ years of combined experience in Procurement/Supply Chain Management or Engineering
  • 5+ years of experience in the automotive industry, with deep specialization in one or more commodity categories
  • Demonstrated ownership of complex, high-value, or multiple categories, including setting category strategy
  • Experience independently negotiating complex, multi-million-dollar supply contracts
  • Track record of delivering enterprise-level cost reduction targets across categories
  • Experience driving commodity strategy and risk mitigation, such as forward contracting and index-linked pricing

Skills & Competencies

  • Knowledge and experience with ERP/MRP systems (e.g., SAP, Plex, Oracle, NetSuite)
  • Advanced skills in Microsoft Excel for data analysis, cost modeling, pivot tables, and reporting
  • Intermediate+ skills in using AI tools to enhance procurement workflows and analytics
  • Strong analytical, strategic-thinking, and interpersonal skills, including the ability to build and present business cases to senior leadership
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for cross-functional, executive, and supplier interaction
  • Ability to mentor Buyer I and Buyer II team members and informally lead category teams
  • Ability to identify process issues and drive improvements to improve operational efficiency
  • High level of integrity and ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced start-up environment
  • CPSM, CPM, or equivalent professional certification preferred

WHY JOIN TEAM SLATE?

At Slate, we’re fueled by grit, determination, and attention to detail. The start-up spirit of ingenuity and resourcefulness move our business forward. Team Slate fosters a culture of excellence, innovation, and mutual respect, and is motivated by shared principles.

  • Safety First

  • Delight Customers

  • Fast, Frugal, and Scrappy

  • Respectful Collaboration

  • Positive Legacy

Job Description Summary

Lamb Weston’s Senior Specialist – ESG Engagement will support the Company’s growing interaction with internal and external stakeholders. This position will participate in and/or lead a variety of internal and external activities including cross functional collaboration with other ESG resources, the Company’s Supply Chain and Commercial teams, customers, suppliers, and ESG rating, ranking and certification systems. Along with the Sr. Director, ESG Administration this position will ensure Lamb Weston’s ESG strategy and programs are moving forward, and progress is represented accurately and consistently across various audiences.




Responsibilities include supporting and tracking ESG activities across other business functions, collaborating with Communications and Marketing to enhance internal and external ESG messaging, and tracking and responding to various forms of external requests for ESG information.

Job Description


  • Support and aid in development of ESG and Sustainability initiatives and programs.
  • Contribute to internal programs by providing support as an ESG Subject Matter Expert.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to ensure ESG messaging is consistently and accurately conveyed to all stakeholders (internal and external).
  • Represent ESG interests within EHS Pillar Teams and/or Green Teams ensuring appropriate level of focus and facilitating best practice sharing.
  • Work with Lamb Weston ESG Team Members as well as key internal customers, including Global Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Ag Services, Capital Management, and Corporate Finance groups to support and track strategy and roadmap deliverables.
  • Collaborate with Sr. Director, ESG Administration to track and consolidate qualitative ESG activities across the Company.
  • Lead tactical external engagement activities including customer inquiries, questionnaires, ESG related rating/ranking systems, and certification or audit programs.

title: Executive Director - Cash Management Germany
description:
Excited to grow your career?

BBVA is a global company with more than 160 years of history that operates in more than 25 countries where we serve more than 80 million customers. We are more than 121,000 professionals working in multidisciplinary teams with profiles as diverse as financiers, legal experts, data scientists, developers, engineers and designers.

We are looking for a senior Cash Management professional with 10/15 years of experience within leading international banks, combining strong product expertise with a proven commercial track record in the German Corporate and Institutional market.


The successful candidate will be responsible for building and scaling BBVA's local Cash Management franchise in Germany while continuing to accelerate Inbound and Outbound business across BBVA's global network.


The role requires deep expertise across Payments, Collections, Liquidity Management and Connectivity, together with strong client relationships, product development experience, commercial leadership and the ability to operate effectively across a complex international organization.


About the job:

International Banking Experience

  • Minimum 10-15 years of experience in Cash Management / Transaction Banking within a leading international bank.
  • Strong understanding of the German Corporate, Institutional and Transaction Banking market.
  • Experience working within international and matrix organizations.
  • Strong network across German Corporates, Financial Institutions, Treasury Centers and the broader treasury ecosystem.
  • Experience in management of projects will be highly valued.

Cash Management Product Expertise

  • Deep knowledge of Accounts, Payments, Collections and Liquidity Management.
  • Strong understanding of the German and European payments environment and relevant domestic payment infrastructure.
  • Experience with connectivity solutions including APIs, Host-to-Host, SWIFT and ERP/TMS integration, and local bank agnostic platforms.
  • Knowledge of international liquidity solutions, including Cash Pooling, intercompany payments and cash forecasting.
  • Experience identifying product gaps and working with Product and Engineering teams to develop new capabilities, and translating client needs into commercial product priorities.

Commercial & Client Coverage

  • Proven track record in selling sophisticated Cash Management solutions to Corporate and Institutional clients.
  • Ability to engage credibly with CFOs, Group Treasurers, Treasury Centers and senior finance executives.
  • Experience leading RFPs and complex regional/global Cash Management mandates.
  • Strong capabilities in pipeline management, pricing, negotiation and conversion.

Job Description

  • Define and execute the German Cash Management Strategic Plan.
  • Build and lead the local Cash Management team.
  • Define the target coverage model and client segmentation.
  • Establish commercial targets and KPIs.
  • Coordinate closely with CIB Bankers and embed Cash Management into their commercial routines.
  • Represent Germany within the Global Cash Management organization.
  • Coordinate Product, Implementation, Client Service, Operations, Engineering, Compliance, Legal, Risk and Finance.
  • Drive the development of the local product proposition.
  • Identify strategic partnerships where appropriate.
  • Monitor revenues, balances & deposits, transaction volumes, profitability and budget execution.

title: Business Systems Analyst
description:
Chiesi USA

Chiesi USA is a commercial affiliate of the Chiesi Group.

Chiesi is an international research-focused biopharmaceutical group with 90 years’ experience, operating in more than 30 countries, with its Headquarter in Parma, Italy. More than 8,000 employees across the group are united by a singular purpose: promoting a healthier world for our people, patients, and the planet. This is what drives us as we research, develop, and market innovative drugs across our main therapeutic areas. Discover more here.

At Chiesi we are thinking generations ahead, driving sustainable innovation with purpose. This fosters a culture of reliability, transparency, and ethical behavior at every level. As a Benefit Corporation and a certified B Corp, we have embedded sustainability in our bylaws and continuously measure our impact.

Diversity and inclusion are at the heart of who we are. We believe our differences make us stronger. We are a vibrant ecosystem of passionate, talented individuals united by strong values, each bringing unique perspectives that help us to continuously challenge the status quo for the better.

Who we are looking for

This is what you will do

The Business Systems Analyst serves as a strategic liaison between business stakeholders and IT, responsible for building strong business partnerships, eliciting and documenting business requirements and processes, translating requirements into functional specifications, and overseeing the successful delivery of projects and application enhancements throughout the system development lifecycle.

This role combines business analysis, project coordination, and stakeholder management responsibilities to ensure technology solutions align with business objectives and deliver measurable value. The Business Systems Analyst will proactively engage business partners to identify opportunities for process improvement, prioritize initiatives, and drive continuous optimization of global and local applications.

Candidates must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Sponsorship for employment-based visas, now or in the future, is not available for this position

You’ll be responsible for:

1. Business Analysis

  • Analyze current-state ("as-is") and future-state ("to-be") processes, and identify the gaps, risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Translate business requirements into clear, complete, and actionable functional specifications and ensure alignment between business and technical teams to make certain they are accurately understood and implemented
  • Coordinate and/or facilitate user acceptance testing, documenting and triaging defects, and confirming the delivered solution meets the documented acceptance criteria.
  • Distinguish between stated wants and underlying needs, and challenge requirements constructively where a simpler or more standard solution would serve the business better.
  • Evaluate solution options — configuration, enhancement, third-party solution, process change — and make recommendations with a supporting rationale.

2. Project & Enhancement Delivery

  • Plan and manage small-to-medium projects and enhancement efforts end to end - scope, schedule, resource needs, dependencies, and deliverables.
  • Coordinate across internal development teams, infrastructure, QA, vendors, and business resources to keep work moving.
  • Monitor and provide clear status reports throughout the execution across the application development lifecycle, tracking progress against plan and flagging risks and issues early with proposed mitigations.
  • Manage scope actively — assess the impact of change requests and routes them through the appropriate approval path aligned with the corporate governance model.
  • Ensure deliverables are completed on schedule and meet quality expectations.

3. Business Partnership & Stakeholder Management

  • Serve as the primary ICT point of contact for assigned business functions, facilitating regular discussions with stakeholders and process owners to understand current pain points, upcoming initiatives, and strategic direction to identify opportunities for process improvements, automation, and system enhancements
  • Communicate effectively with audiences ranging from end users to senior leadership, adjusting technical depth to the audience.
  • Act as an advocate for business needs while ensuring alignment with ICT strategy, governance, and architectural standards.
  • Proactively identify opportunities where technology can reduce manual effort, improve data quality, or support growth

4. Demand Management

  • Assist in the evaluation of business value, complexity, cost, risk, and strategic alignment of proposed initiatives.
  • Assist in prioritizing demand against other projects and enhancements within the ICT portfolio.
  • Support annual planning and roadmap development activities.

You will need to have

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Systems, Business Administration, Computer Science, or a related field.
  • 3–5+ years of experience as a business systems analyst, business analyst, or in a comparable role supporting enterprise business applications.
  • Demonstrated experience eliciting requirements from non-technical stakeholders and producing functional specifications that development teams can build from.
  • Experience supporting application enhancement and projects across a full software development lifecycle, from ideation to deployment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to business audiences and business context to technical teams.
  • Experience supporting enterprise applications such as ERP, CRM, Quality, Supply Chain, Finance, or Commercial systems.

We would prefer for you to have

  • Experience in the pharmaceutical, biotech, medical device, or another regulated life sciences environment.
  • Experience with validated systems and GxP computer system validation
  • Familiarity with regulated-industry business processes such as manufacturing, quality, clinical, regulatory, supply chain, or commercial operations.
  • Hands-on experience with enterprise platforms such as SAP, Veeva, and SalesForce.
  • Experience with Waterfall, Agile, or Hybrid delivery approaches.
  • Proficiency with tools such as Jira, ServiceNow, Smartsheet, or Visio

Location

Hybrid position based in Cary, NC. #LI-Hybrid

What we offer

No matter where your path starts at Chiesi, it leads to inspiring possibilities. Your future is our focus, and we are committed to nurturing your development in our dynamic, friendly environment with access to resources and training every step of the way.
We provide top-class benefits, including comprehensive healthcare programs, work-life balance initiatives, and robust relocation support. description:
Be visionary

Teledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.​

We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.

Job Description

Teledyne Energetics is comprised of Teledyne Electronic Safety Products (TESP) and Teledyne RISI Inc. (RISI). TESP specializes in developing solid state Electronic Safe & Arms for Military, Space, and Commercial (Oil Exploration/Production). RISI specializes in developing EBW and EFI detonators that integrate into Electronic Safe & Arms.

Teledyne RISI is seeking a detail-oriented and highly organized Production / Compliance Leader to support daily manufacturing operations while ensuring regulatory compliance, production traceability, and inventory accountability. This role serves as a critical link between Production, Quality, Planning, and Materials Management to ensure efficient workflow execution, accurate documentation, and compliance with ATF and company requirements.

The ideal candidate possesses strong organizational skills, a commitment to accuracy, and experience working within a regulated manufacturing environment where documentation, traceability, and material control are essential to operational success.

Responsibilities:

Production Compliance & Documentation

  • Maintain all ATF records and logs in accordance with federal regulations and company procedures.

  • Monitor production activities to ensure compliance with regulatory, customer, and internal quality requirements.

  • Support internal and external audits by maintaining accurate and complete documentation.

  • Assist in the development and implementation of process improvements related to compliance and production controls.

  • Ensure manufacturing records are complete, accurate, and properly retained.

Work Order Management & Traceability

  • Review and verify manufacturing work orders for completeness and accuracy.

  • Ensure all required manufacturing and inspection sign-offs are completed.

  • Maintain process traceability throughout all stages of production.

  • Verify route sheets, travelers, and production documentation are properly completed and controlled.

  • Work with Production, Quality, and Engineering personnel to resolve documentation discrepancies.

Material Management & WIP Control

  • Issue production kits and materials to manufacturing personnel.

  • Track Work-In-Process (WIP) inventory throughout the manufacturing cycle.

  • Maintain accurate inventory transactions and material traceability records.

  • Coordinate material movements to support production schedules and minimize disruptions.

  • Assist with inventory reconciliations, cycle counts, and material audits.

Product Labeling & Identification

  • Create and print product, lot, packaging, and shipping labels.

  • Verify labeling accuracy and compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.

  • Maintain controlled label templates and associated records.

  • Ensure proper identification of all materials and finished products throughout the manufacturing process.

Production Planning & Resource Support

  • Support the Production Supervisor in daily production planning and scheduling activities.

  • Assist with resource allocation to support on-time manufacturing objectives.

  • Monitor production progress and identify potential bottlenecks.

  • Communicate material shortages, production delays, and compliance concerns to management.

  • Participate in continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, efficiency, and quality.

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.

  • Associate degree in Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

  • Minimum five (5) years of experience in manufacturing, inventory control, materials management, production control, or compliance-related functions.

  • Experience working in a regulated manufacturing environment preferred.

  • Working knowledge of manufacturing processes and production documentation.

  • Familiarity with inventory management and material control practices.

  • Understanding of traceability requirements and work order management.

  • Experience with ERP/MRP business systems and proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.

  • Strong organizational, time-management, written communication, and verbal communication skills.

  • Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

  • Ability to regularly stand, walk, bend, and perform tasks within a manufacturing environment.

  • Ability to occasionally lift and move materials up to 25 pounds.

  • Ability to perform computer and administrative tasks for extended periods.

  • Must be 21 or older

  • Able to pass the ATF background check

title: F-35/5th Generation Fighter Pilot Subject Matter Expert (SME)
description:
Our instructor pilots strengthen safety and readiness by preparing military aviators for critical missions. Your experience helps new recruits perform at their best when the stakes are highest. Join a team powered by cutting-edge technology and a shared commitment to empowering defence forces worldwide.

Description

Shape the Future of Fighter Pilot Training in Canada

CAE is seeking an experienced F-35 / 5th Generation Fighter Pilot Subject Matter Expert (SME) to support the design and delivery of Canada’s Future Fighter Lead-In Training (FFLIT) program.

This opportunity allows you to leverage your operational and instructional experience to influence how the next generation of Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) fighter pilots are prepared for the F-35. Working alongside military stakeholders, training developers, and aviation experts, you will help define training concepts, develop courseware, and shape a fighter training ecosystem built around the Leonardo M-346 platform.

This is a non-flying role focused on training development, operational design, and program implementation.

As the program’s F-35 / 5th Generation fighter expert, you will serve as a key advisor supporting the design, development, validation, and implementation of the FFLIT training system.

Duties & Responsibilities:


Training Development

  • Provide operational expertise to support the design and development of classroom, simulator, and flying training curricula
  • Review and validate courseware to ensure accuracy, relevance, and alignment with RCAF training objectives
  • Support acceptance testing of courseware and training devices
  • Contribute to training policies, procedures, and instructional standards
  • Identify training risks and support validation and verification activities

Operational and Program Advisory

  • Advise on the integration of F-35 operational concepts into the FFLIT curriculum and training ecosystem.
  • Support the development of concepts of operations, training centre procedures, and operational policies.
  • Collaborate with CAE teams, RCAF stakeholders, and program leadership to achieve key program milestones.
  • Provide expert input on Ground-Based Training Systems (GBTS), simulator utilization, and future training capability development.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Operational experience as an F-35 or other 5th Generation fighter pilot and instructor pilot within the RCAF or a comparable military organization.
  • 10–15 years of military flight operations experience.
  • 10+ years of leadership or instructional experience.
  • Experience with simulator-based and synthetic training environments.
  • Experience supporting curriculum development, instructional systems design, or military training program management.
  • Strong collaboration and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Postsecondary education in a relevant discipline.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Level II Security Clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Former F-35 Instructor Pilot or Instructor Pilot on another 5th Generation platform.
  • Experience within RCAF fighter training and training development organizations.
  • M-346, FLIT, or advanced jet training experience.
  • Experience supporting simulator, training device, or GBTS development and acceptance testing.
  • Experience developing operational policies and procedures.
  • Bilingualism in English and French is considered an asset.

Benefits

We’ve designed flexible policies to promote well-being and growth, based on role-specific eligibility and requirements:

  • Flexible hybrid work arrangement from anywhere in Canada.
  • Occasional travel within Canada, including Ottawa and Cold Lake, with limited international travel as required
  • Opportunity to contribute directly to one of Canada’s significant military aviation training initiatives
  • Opportunity to work with experts in simulation, training, and mission readiness while helping shape how future RCAF fighter pilots are prepared for operational service in the F-35 era.

title: Senior Scientist, Formulation Delivery Systems
description:
Senior Scientist, Delivery Technologies


CSL's organization is accelerating innovation to deliver greater impact for patients. With a project-led structure and a focus on collaboration, we're building a future-ready team that thrives in dynamic biotech ecosystems. Joining CSL now means being part of an agile team committed to developing therapies that make a meaningful difference worldwide.

Could you be our next Senior Scientist, Delivery Technologies?


Work Environment:


This position is based in Waltham, MA and is an onsite role 5 days each week. CSL is not providing relocation assistance or visa sponsorship.


You will report to the Principal Scientist, Delivery Technologies


The successful candidate will provide scientific expertise in the design, formulation, characterization, and optimization of delivery technologies to support drug discovery efforts across multiple functions and external collaborations. This role requires strong expertise in lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation, extra-hepatic targeted delivery approaches, siRNA-conjugates to enable tissue- and cell-specific delivery, and extensive knowledge in translational drug delivery sciences.


Key Responsibilities


  • Contribute and support CSL’s novel modalities portfolio and pipeline
  • Participate in external due diligence, assessing delivery system suitability for various modalities, technical feasibility, and risk
  • Lead the design, formulation, and characterization of LNPs containing siRNA, mRNA, gene-editing cargoes, and other nucleic acid modalities
  • Design and execute Design of Experiment (DOE) principles in formulation screening
  • Work on medium to high throughput formulation preparation
  • Optimize formulation parameters, lipid composition, manufacturing processes, and excipient systems to enhance stability and biological performance
  • Develop and characterize targeted delivery strategies (t-LNP) utilizing receptor-mediated uptake mechanisms, targeting ligands, and tissue-specific delivery approaches
  • Lead efforts related to the design and evaluation of ligand-siRNA conjugates for extrahepatic delivery
  • Evaluate delivery performance through in vitro and in vivo studies, including cellular uptake, endosomal escape, biodistribution, and target engagement
  • Serve as a subject matter expert in delivery approaches and LNP process development, and provide technical delivery-related support across research, development, and manufacturing activities
  • Apply mechanistic insights into critical process parameters and product attributes through hypothesis-driven experimentation, robust data analysis, and problem-solving
  • Provide scientific guidance and mentorship to team members and collaborate closely with Analytical Biochemistry and Molecular Biology teams

Minimum Qualifications:


  • PhD with 5+ years or MS with 7+ years of relevant experience in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Nanomedicine, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Drug Delivery, in the pharmaceutical industry
  • Demonstrated ability to independently lead scientific projects and experience working in cross-functional research environments
  • Strong track record in LNP formulation and optimization
  • Expertise in nanoparticle characterization techniques including particle size, encapsulation efficiency, and stability assessment
  • Expertise in in vitro and in vivo evaluation of RNA-based delivery systems
  • Understanding of cellular uptake mechanisms, intracellular trafficking, and endosomal escape
  • Demonstrated experience with targeted LNPs and extrahepatic delivery platforms
  • Experimental design, statistical analysis, and data interpretation
  • Preferred: Knowledge of medicinal chemistry principles related to ionizable lipid design, structure-activity relationships (SAR), ligand optimization and linker chemistry

The minimum and maximum base salary range that CSL expects to pay for this position at the Waltham, MA USA work location at the time of this posting is $126,000/yr - $157,000/yr. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.


CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

title: Sr. Director, New Product Planning, Oncology
description:
The Role
Building on the success of our platform in infectious diseases and positive INT data, Moderna is expanding its footprint in oncology. We are seeking a Senior Director of New Product Planning for our early oncology programs, from discovery through clinical proof of concept.


The Senior Director will shape product and development strategy across the early oncology portfolio. They will connect each program’s mechanism of action with disease biology to identify where it could deliver meaningful clinical benefit and change treatment decisions. Working with program leaders and colleagues across Research, Development, Commercial, and Manufacturing, they will translate that opportunity into target product profiles, indication and development choices, and recommendations on how programs and opportunities should be prioritized across the portfolio.


The successful candidate will bring demonstrated ability to lead program and portfolio strategy and a systems-thinking approach to integrating scientific, clinical, and market evidence. They will frame choices, lead cross-functional debate, and present recommendations to senior leaders on which opportunities to advance and where to focus investment and resources before development paths are fully defined.


Here’s What You’ll Do
Scientific and disease understanding

  • Develop a deep understanding of Moderna’s platform and its application to oncology.
  • Work with scientific and clinical colleagues to assess how each program’s mechanism of action could affect disease, including the implications of tumor biology, patient heterogeneity, and biomarkers.
  • Independently evaluate mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence and its implications for program strategy, including disease progression and clinical endpoints.
  • Engage directly with scientific evidence and external experts to evaluate competing hypotheses and identify unresolved biological questions that affect development choices.

Market and competitive understanding

  • Understand how patients move through diagnosis, staging, biomarker testing, treatment selection, assessment, and subsequent treatment. Identify who makes each decision and how clinical evidence, physician judgment, patient preferences, and access shape those choices, including unmet needs within current standards of care.
  • Integrate market and competitive expertise into early program decisions.
  • Evaluate approved therapies, emerging mechanisms, and competitor programs, including their clinical evidence, development timelines, and potential strengths and limitations.
  • Develop scenarios for how standards of care and treatment pathways may evolve, including changes in treatment sequencing and the requirements for future differentiation.
  • Use direct conversations with KOLs, treating physicians, and other internal and external experts, together with scientific and market evidence, to test program assumptions and resolve questions that affect development choices.

Product and development strategy

  • Lead a disciplined strategy process with program teams: frame the choices, identify the information needed, structure debate around alternatives and tradeoffs, and make the logic for program decisions explicit.
  • Apply a biotech investment mindset to program development, identifying the most efficient path to reduce key risks and reach proof of concept. Define the evidence needed to justify further investment and adapt recommendations as data emerge.
  • Shape strategy and prioritization across the early oncology portfolio. Develop and present recommendations to senior leaders on which opportunities to advance and where to focus investment and resources, with clear alternatives, tradeoffs, and evidence gaps.
  • Integrate scientific, disease, market, and competitive insights to define where each oncology program can succeed and prioritize indications, patient populations, treatment settings, and lines of therapy.
  • Develop and refine target product profiles with program teams that connect the program’s mechanism of action and disease biology to a defined patient population, treatment setting, and clinical benefit. Define the efficacy, safety, durability, and dosing and administration requirements, together with the supporting evidence, needed for differentiation and to change treatment choices as standards of care evolve.
  • Shape clinical and evidence-generation plans, including patient selection, biomarkers, endpoints, and the evidence required for regulatory approval, physician adoption, reimbursement, and access.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Basic Qualifications)

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in a scientific, medical, business, or related field.
  • At least 10 years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including significant experience in new product planning, research strategy, program leadership, global marketing, portfolio strategy, or a related function.
  • Demonstrated experience leading product and portfolio strategy across multiple programs in discovery and early clinical development, including influencing senior decisions on program advancement, investment, and resource allocation.
  • Strong understanding of oncology biology and clinical development, with the ability to independently evaluate mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence and connect it to treatment decisions.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience in oncology, including familiarity with treatment pathways, clinical endpoints, patient segmentation, and the evolving competitive landscape.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to build, challenge, and communicate assumptions.
  • Demonstrated ability to use AI-supported evidence workflows to investigate program questions, test competing explanations, evaluate underlying sources, and identify when expert input or additional data is needed.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present a concise recommendation to senior leaders and defend it objectively.
  • The ability to influence across functions without direct authority, lead teams through competing views, and establish productive working relationships with scientific, clinical, and commercial colleagues.

Our Working Model
As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model. This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.


Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.


Pay & Benefits

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

  • Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
  • A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
  • Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
  • Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
  • Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
  • Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $196,700.00 - $353,400.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.

About Moderna

Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.


By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.


We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.


If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.

We’re focused on attracting, retaining, developing, and advancing our employees. By cultivating a workplace that values diverse experiences, backgrounds, and ideas, we create an environment where every employee can contribute their best.

title: IT SAP Time Management Functional Analyst
description:
At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit . Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Welcome to BWXT

We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

Position Overview:

This role focuses on SAP Time Management configuration. SAP CATS is used at BWXT for time entry and approval. Time Evaluation is used for various premium pay situations and quota determination. This position will work with the development team to deliver reports, enhancements, forms, interfaces, IDOC/ALE integration. They will also release transports for migration to the QA system, defining and executing test plan to assure proper application functioning.

Location:

Remote with travel

Your Day to Day as an IT SAP Time Management Functional Analyst:

Requirement Analysis & Solution Delivery:

  • Gather business requirements; plan, design, test, train, and deploy SAP Time Management solutions.
  • Configure and test SAP CATS Time Management, work schedules, shifts, absence quotas, and timekeeping enhancements.
  • Configure and test Time Evaluation, including schema and rule changes.
  • Support integration with external time-entry applications (e.g., Jamis, Autotime).
  • Understand and manage Time Management integration points with other SAP modules.

Support & Issue Resolution

  • Investigate and resolve helpdesk tickets related to:
    • CATS timekeeping and Time Evaluation.
    • Approval workflows tied to the HR organizational structure.
  • Provide time-related support to local timekeepers and payroll teams.

Project Participation

  • Contribute to larger initiatives involving SAP timekeeping, such as system consolidations, acquisition integrations, and organizational growth.
  • Work within an environment that includes a separate SAP HCM system and IDoc transfers of employee and organizational data to SAP ECC.
  • Support a custom effective rate program for billing and project cost control.

Collaboration

  • Partner with SAP developers, other functional teams, and business intelligence teams to deliver solutions.
  • Work with business stakeholders to understand and document project and manufacturing process requirements.

User Training & Support

  • Provide training on new or updated processes.
  • Offer ongoing guidance to ensure smooth system operation.

Documentation

  • Create thorough documentation for SAP configurations, processes, and solutions.
  • Maintain up-to-date materials for future reference and training.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to enhance system functionality and business processes.
  • Stay current on SAP updates, tools, and best practices.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant SAP configuration experience with a focus on Time Management.
  • Proven experience as an SAP ERP Functional Analyst.
  • Strong communications skills and customer orientation.
  • Significant troubleshooting skills as well as the ability to adapt quickly to new systems and technologies.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communications and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team and independently when required.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) clearance.

Preferred Additional Qualifications:

  • SAP certification in Time Management.

title: VP, Product Management - Industrial Solutions
description:
Work Model: You’ll work in a hybrid model, onsite at your designated Regal Rexnord location at least 3 days per week (Monday–Thursday), with flexibility to work remotely up to 2 days, including Friday.

____________________

The PES Americas division, a ~$1.1B global business within the Power and Efficiency Solutions (PES) Segment of Regal Rexnord, is seeking a Vice President of Product Management for our Industrial Solutions Motors business unit. This is a critical role to both create and drive a growth-focused product strategy.


Reporting to the President, PES Americas division, this role will have responsibility for the overall strategy and execution of the Industrial Solutions business unit. The Vice President of Product Management is responsible for defining and executing the product strategy, portfolio roadmap, and innovation agenda for the business. This executive leader drives profitable growth, market share expansion, and customer satisfaction through a disciplined product management process spanning the entire product lifecycle.


The role partners closely with Engineering, Sales, Marketing, Operations, Finance, and Business Leadership to identify market opportunities, translate customer needs into differentiated solutions, and ensure successful commercialization of new and existing products. The Vice President of Product Management develops high-performing product management teams and champions a culture of innovation, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer-centric decision making.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Define and execute clear, multi-year product strategies and roadmaps aligned with overall business goals and market opportunities. Ensure the product portfolio roadmap supports the company’s strategic objectives and adapts to industry trends and customer needs.
  • Manage the entire life cycle of the Industrial Solutions Motors product lines within the division, from concept to end-of-life. Prioritize new product development and enhancements, manage portfolio mix and ensure timely, successful product launches and transitions.
  • Drive and own the ~300M P&L for the Industrial Solutions business unit, with accountability for driving product portfolio revenue growth, profitability and ROI. Develop business cases, influence pricing and investment decisions, and monitor portfolio performance against financial targets.
  • Champion a customer-centric approach. Leverage voice-of-customer, market research, and competitive intelligence to inform product direction and segment-specific offerings. Anticipate market shifts and ensure the portfolio meets evolving customer needs in each target segment.
  • Partner cross-functionally to deliver high-quality products and solutions to market on time and at scale. Align cross-functional efforts to product plans, ensuring manufacturability, quality, and a successful go-to-market execution for each segment.
  • Drive continuous improvement of the planning and delivery of products and solutions through the use of the Regal Rexnord Business System (RBS), which includes application of the 80/20 framework.
  • Build and lead a high-performing product management team by engaging, coaching, and developing team members. Set clear goals, provide mentorship, and develop talent. Foster a culture of accountability and collaboration ensuring the organization has the capabilities to execute product and segment strategies effectively.

Minimum Requirements:


  • Bachelor’s degree from an Accredited University required
  • Minimum 12 years of commercial, product or marketing experience with highly engineered products in a complex B2B industrial manufacturing enterprise
  • Proven ability to lead both direct and cross-functional teams and influence in a global structure
  • Strong financial acumen, executive presence, and the ability to lead multiple projects and teams
  • Able to balance strategic solution planning with hands-on execution and delivery.
  • Proficiency with MS Office (Excel / Word / Power Point) and CRM (i.e. SalesForce.com or Microsoft Dynamics)
  • Must have the ability to digest commercial transaction data to manage the product families and identify trends/issues (i.e., Power BI)
  • Must be able to travel at least 30% of the time domestically and internationally as required.
  • Demonstrates the Regal Rexnord Values; Integrity, Responsibility, Diversity, Engagement & Inclusion, Customer Success, Innovation with Purpose, Continuous Improvement, Performance, Passion to Win, and Sense of Urgency
  • Relevant industry experience, typically Food & Beverage, Materials Handling/Conveying, and/or Industrial Equipment spaces

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Advanced degree (MS Engineering, MBA, etc.)
  • Experience in Agile Product Management teams
  • Experience of NPD stage gate and/or portfolio management systems/software
  • Hands-on experience with the 80/20 process and product line simplification

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescription Drug Coverage
  • Spending accounts (HSA, Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA)
  • Paid Time Off and Holidays
  • 401k Retirement Plan with Matching Employer Contributions
  • Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance
  • Paid Leaves
  • Tuition Assistance


About Regal Rexnord

Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.


The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.


Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. Regal Rexnord has offices and manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. For more information, including a copy of our Sustainability Report, visit RegalRexnord.com.

Key Responsibilities

  • Stitching & Assembly: Reading tie-down material lists and assembly prints to stitch tie downs with required hardware. You’ll also inspect, fold, and package completed tie downs per Company and customer specifications.
  • Operating Equipment: Using production equipment such as automatic folders, hot knives, and riveters, while ensuring proper safety protocols are followed.
  • Quality Control: Inspecting materials, trimming, and ensuring all tie downs meet quality standards.
  • Efficiency & Continuous Improvement: Working with senior team members and supervisors to meet production goals and improve efficiency.
  • Adhering to ISO Standards: Ensuring compliance with ISO procedures for quality and safety.

  • Documentation: Completing paperwork accurately, including routine job reports and other required forms.

  • Mechanical Aptitude: Ability to use hand tools, measuring devices, and work with small parts (e.g., threads, needles).
  • Mathematical Skills: Competence in basic math (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division) and working with fractions or decimals.

Physical Demands: The role requires frequent use of hands for working with small components, standing, sitting, bending, and occasionally lifting heavier items.

Work Environment: You will work around moving mechanical parts and machines, with potential exposure to chemicals and materials. Safety procedures must be followed at all times. The environment is typically moderate in noise.

As a key player in our production process, you will assist welders and welding supervisors during critical welding operations, ensuring that all activities align with customer contract requirements and industry standards.

Your expertise will guide the development and review of welding procedures, determine and procure necessary weld filler metals, and assist in the design and acquisition of welding equipment.   • Determine weld filler metal needs, order, and release the correct filler metal to welding activities.

title: Sr. Director, New Product Planning, Autoimmune
description:
The Role
Building on the success of our mRNA platform in infectious diseases and the growing clinical evidence in oncology, Moderna is expanding into autoimmune diseases. We are seeking a Senior Director of New Product Planning to shape the strategy for our autoimmune programs and help translate our platform into medicines for patients.


The Senior Director will shape product and development strategy across the autoimmune portfolio. They will connect each program’s mechanism of action with disease biology to identify where it could deliver meaningful clinical benefit and change treatment decisions. They will translate that opportunity into target product profiles, indication and development choices, and recommendations on how programs and opportunities should be prioritized across the portfolio. Working with program leaders and colleagues across Research, Development, Commercial, and Manufacturing, they will lead strategic discussions from discovery through clinical proof of concept.


The successful candidate will bring a deep understanding of autoimmune disease biology and the ability to independently evaluate mechanisms and clinical evidence. They will bring a systems-thinking approach, connecting scientific evidence with patient populations, treatment decisions, regulatory requirements, and evolving market and competitive dynamics to shape program and portfolio strategy. They will provide an independent perspective in areas of uncertainty and present recommendations to senior leaders on which opportunities to advance and where to focus investment and resources before development and commercial paths are fully defined.


Here’s What You’ll Do
Scientific and disease understanding

  • Develop a deep understanding of Moderna’s platform and its application to autoimmune diseases.
  • Develop a deep, independent understanding of autoimmune disease biology, patient heterogeneity, and biomarkers, and assess how each program’s mechanism of action could affect the disease.
  • Assess clinical, translational, and biomarker evidence and develop a detailed understanding of diagnosis, disease progression, and clinical endpoints.
  • Engage directly with scientific evidence and external experts to evaluate competing hypotheses and identify unresolved biological questions.

Market and competitive understanding

  • Understand how patients move from diagnosis and referral through treatment selection, assessment, switching, and discontinuation. Identify who makes each decision and how clinical evidence, physician judgment, patient preferences, and access shape those choices, including unmet needs within current standards of care.
  • Evaluate approved therapies, emerging mechanisms, and competitor programs, including their clinical evidence, development timelines, and potential strengths and limitations.
  • Develop scenarios for how standards of care and treatment pathways may evolve, including changes in treatment sequencing and the requirements for future differentiation.
  • Use direct conversations with KOLs, treating physicians, and other internal and external experts, together with scientific and market evidence, to test program assumptions and resolve questions that affect development choices.

Product and development strategy

  • Lead a disciplined strategy process with program teams: frame the choices, identify the information needed, structure debate around alternatives and tradeoffs, and make the logic for program decisions explicit.
  • Apply a biotech investment mindset to program development, identifying the most efficient path to reduce key risks and reach proof of concept. Define the evidence needed to justify further investment and adapt recommendations as data emerge.
  • Shape strategy and prioritization across the autoimmune portfolio. Develop and present recommendations to senior leaders on which opportunities to advance and where to focus investment and resources, with clear alternatives, tradeoffs, and evidence gaps.
  • Integrate scientific, disease, market, and competitive insights to define where each autoimmune program can succeed and prioritize indications, patient populations, treatment settings, and lines of therapy.
  • Develop and refine target product profiles with program teams that connect the program’s mechanism of action and disease biology to a defined patient population, treatment setting, and clinical benefit. Define the efficacy, safety, durability, and dosing and administration requirements, together with the supporting evidence, needed for differentiation and to change treatment choices as standards of care evolve.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Basic Qualifications)

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in a scientific, medical, business, or related field.
  • At least 10 years of experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry, including significant experience in new product planning, research strategy, program leadership, global marketing, portfolio strategy, or a related function.
  • Demonstrated experience leading product and portfolio strategy across multiple programs in discovery and early clinical development, including influencing senior decisions on program advancement, investment, and resource allocation.
  • Deep understanding of autoimmune disease biology and the ability to independently evaluate mechanistic, translational, and clinical evidence.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

  • Experience in autoimmune or immune-mediated diseases, including familiarity with treatment pathways, clinical endpoints, patient segmentation, and the evolving competitive landscape.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to build, challenge, and communicate assumptions.
  • Demonstrated ability to use AI-supported evidence workflows to investigate program questions, test competing explanations, evaluate underlying sources, and identify when expert input or additional data is needed.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present a concise recommendation to senior leaders and defend it objectively.
  • The ability to influence across functions without direct authority and establish productive working relationships with scientific, clinical, and commercial colleagues.

Our Working Model
As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model. This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.


Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.


Pay & Benefits

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

  • Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
  • A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
  • Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
  • Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
  • Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
  • Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $196,700.00 - $353,400.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs.

The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.

About Moderna

Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.


By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.


We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.


If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.

title: Senior Digital R&D Scientist
description:
To thrive as a Senior Digital R&D Scientist, you will combine a strong foundation in scientific research with a passion for data-driven innovation and the ability to translate emerging technologies into practical R&D solutions. This role brings together coating and formulation science with computational modeling, advanced analytics, and digital innovation to accelerate product development and improve scientific decision-making. As part of the Digitalization & Formula Management team, you will transform formulation data into actionable insights while advancing the use of machine learning, laboratory automation, and modern approaches. We value curiosity, collaboration, creativity, and scientific rigor, and believe the future of R&D is driven by the combination of technical knowledge and digital capabilities!


In this role, you will partner with formulation scientists and cross-functional teams to design and optimize experiments, develop predictive models, analyze datasets, and create digital tools that improve the speed and effectiveness of product development. You will also connect scientific data across R&D systems, translate technical challenges into digital solutions, and help teams adopt new technologies. We rely on this role to lead complex technical initiatives and deliver measurable improvements in R&D productivity, formulation performance, and decision-making. We succeed when innovative thinking, scientific expertise, and technology come together to solve real-world formulation challenges.


Here’s what we’re looking for:


  • High School Diploma required; Bachelor's degree preferred in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Polymer Science, Materials Science, or a related scientific field.
  • 5+ years of experience in scientific R&D, coatings formulation, formulated products, computational science, or related R&D environments.
  • Strong understanding of formulation science, coatings raw materials, formulation principles, performance testing, and structure-property relationships; coatings experience preferred
  • Experience designing and optimizing experiments, analyzing complex technical datasets, and solving scientific and formulation challenges.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects, influence cross-functional teams, mentor scientists, and drive adoption of new tools and methodologies.
  • Proven experience applying Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical analysis, predictive modeling, sequential learning, machine learning, Bayesian optimization, or related computational approaches to scientific problems.
  • Proficiency in Python, R, or comparable programming and data analysis tools, with ability to develop or adapt analytical workflows and models.
  • Experience developing, evaluating, or supporting scientific data platforms, digital R&D workflows, laboratory automation, data integration, or AI-enabled research solutions; familiarity with Uncountable or similar systems preferred.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, teaching, and problem-solving skills with the ability to translate complex findings into actionable recommendations.
  • Develop and apply computational models and AI-enabled tools that leverage formulation, raw material, and performance data to identify relationships, predict outcomes, recommend experiments, and accelerate formulation optimization.

description:
Job Summary/Objective:

Performs responsible, equitable, and professional casework in an inclusive team environment in accordance with established social work/counseling principles. Uses an asset-based approach to engage with the client system in developing and implementing individualized service plans involving the application of casework methods and applicable program policies. Supports and assists clients with safety, personal, family, social, health, and economic needs. Empowers the client/family to attain their highest level of self-sufficiency. As an organization, ACDSS is committed to building a diverse team of contributors who believe and work from the foundation of our core values of equity and inclusion, hope, respect, opportunity, and self-determination. Starting offer is based on applicable education, experience and internal equity.

Essential Functions:

  • Interprets laws, policies and regulations as applied to specific area of responsibility.
  • Assesses cognitive, emotional, and behavioral functioning of children and their families, and develops and implements sophisticated psychosocial case plans which integrate psychodynamic, systemic, medical, and social-ecological intervention approaches.
  • Provides direct counseling, applying family-systems treatment models to complex family situations, in such a way as to strengthen families and prevent family dissolution.
  • Plans, oversees and participates directly in court intervention to protect children and to achieve goals of safety, permanency and well-being of children.
  • Informs clients of specific and related service programs, rules/regulations, and right to participate.
  • Presents cases in supervisory, team and other settings to determine appropriate services and writes/implements service plans.
  • Provides case management services and monitors outcomes of services.
  • Assesses, secures, and monitors financial resources for which the child is eligible (e.g. social security, child support, etc.).
  • Follows the requirements for funding authorization and service payments for services for children and their families.
  • Completes necessary federal, state and local planning and reporting requirements, including documentation entered into OASIS.
  • Coordinates with other agencies and participates in multi-disciplinary and interagency teams providing services to customers.
  • Serves as resource to clients and the community in area of expertise.
  • Provides coverage after hours and on weekends, on a rotating on-call basis, for emergencies involving abuse or neglect of children and adolescents, and for situations requiring immediate attention regarding children in the legal custody of the Department of Social Services.
  • Participates in staffing of emergency shelters as required.
  • Performs other duties as may be assigned.

Competency: Knowledge/ Skills/Abilities:

  • Working knowledge of social work principles and practices;
  • Knowledge of social, economic and health problems; institutions and the methods of the helping process; individual and group behavior.
  • Knowledge of child and adolescent growth and development, family structure and dynamics, the impact of handicapping physical and mental conditions on families, and crisis intervention.
  • Skill in using personal computer with associated software;
  • Ability to identify social problems and needs and to assess the ability to individual and families to utilize services in problem solving;
  • Ability to accept the rights, responsibilities and differences of others;
  • Ability to work effectively through counseling and other methods with individuals and families in helping them solve their problems;
  • Ability to plan and organize work;
  • Ability to understand and interpret laws, policies and regulations;
  • Ability to communicate and establish effective working relationships with clients, coworkers, other professional and technical staff, social agencies and the general public;
  • Ability to plan and organize work;
  • Ability to prepare reports and maintain records.

Required Education and Experience:

  • Minimum of a Bachelor's Degree in a Human Services field or minimum of a Bachelor's Degree in any field and minimum of two years of appropriate and related experience in a Human Services area.
  • Experience in assigned program area and completion of required training programs or equivalent combination of training and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities.

Preferred Qualifications/Certifications:

  • Possession of a BSW or MSW degree and a Commonwealth of Virginia Social Work license are desirable. Masters preferred.

Physical and Mental Requirements:

  • Possession of a valid appropriate driver's permit issued by the Commonwealth of Virginia. Workers in this position are required to drive and they must meet eligibility requirements of the County’s safe driver policy.
  • Administers work to the public, frequently in home settings, including remote rural areas.
  • Involves office-based work for purposes of documentation and data entry. • Frequent contacts with clients and their families; coordination with professionals and representatives of other public and private agencies (i.e. school, courts, clinics, etc.) are required.
  • Involves frequent driving, walking, standing.
  • Must be able to assist physically dependent individuals.

Remote Work:

This position is not eligible for remote work. All County staff must maintain residence within the Commonwealth of Virginia.
