title: Maintenance Assistant - Prime Gastonia
description:
Maintenance Assistant

Take Pride in Maintaining More Than a Community-Help Create an Exceptional Resident Experience!

Prime Independent Living is seeking a hands-on, service-focused Maintenance Assistant to work alongside our Maintenance Director and help keep our community safe, beautiful, and welcoming every day.

As Maintenance Assistant, you'll serve as the right hand to the Maintenance Director, helping with everything from resident service requests and preventive maintenance to apartment turns, grounds, repairs, and day-to-day upkeep. This is a hands-on role where no two days are exactly the same-and your work will directly impact the experience of our residents.

If you're a natural problem-solver who takes pride in your work, enjoys being part of a team, and loves making a difference behind the scenes, we'd love to meet you!

What You'll Do

Maintenance & Community Operations

  • Assist with day-to-day maintenance and repairs throughout apartments, common areas, community buildings, grounds, and parking areas.

  • Respond to resident service requests and complete work orders in a timely, professional manner.

  • Assist with repairs involving HVAC systems, plumbing, electrical, appliances, lighting, and general building maintenance.

  • Help maintain a safe, clean, attractive, and welcoming environment throughout the community.

  • Support the Maintenance Director with daily priorities, projects, and maintenance needs.

Preventive Maintenance & Apartment Turns

  • Assist with scheduled preventive maintenance throughout the community.

  • Help inspect building systems, equipment, apartments, and common areas for needed repairs or maintenance.

  • Support apartment turnovers, including repairs, touch-ups, installations, and other work needed to ensure residences are move-in ready.

  • Assist with routine inspections and maintenance of community equipment and systems.

  • Report maintenance concerns and potential issues to the Maintenance Director.

Vendors, Contractors & Projects

  • Assist the Maintenance Director with coordinating and supporting outside contractors, vendors, and service providers.

  • Provide access and on-site assistance to vendors as needed.

  • Help ensure contracted work is completed safely and with minimal disruption to residents.

  • Assist with community improvement projects, installations, repairs, and other special projects.

Safety & Emergency Preparedness

  • Assist with maintaining emergency equipment and supporting emergency response procedures.

  • Support fire safety initiatives, inspections, and emergency preparedness efforts.

  • Follow company policies, safety standards, and regulatory requirements.

  • Maintain safe work practices and promptly report potential hazards or safety concerns.

Supplies, Tools & Maintenance Areas

  • Help maintain inventory of maintenance supplies, equipment, and tools.

  • Ensure tools and equipment are properly used, maintained, and stored.

  • Assist with receiving and organizing maintenance supplies.

  • Keep maintenance workspaces clean, organized, and safe.

Resident & Team Support

  • Build positive relationships with residents through responsive, courteous, and professional service.

  • Communicate clearly with residents regarding maintenance needs and service requests.

  • Work collaboratively with the Maintenance Director and other departments to support community operations.

  • Assist with special projects, resident events, and operational needs as requested.

  • Serve as a helpful and dependable resource for residents, families, guests, and fellow team members.

What We're Looking For

  • Previous maintenance, facilities, property management, hospitality, senior living, or related experience preferred.

  • Working knowledge of general building maintenance, including basic plumbing, electrical, HVAC, appliance repair, painting, and general repairs.

  • Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.

  • Willingness to learn and take direction from the Maintenance Director.

  • Excellent customer service and communication skills.

  • Ability to prioritize tasks and respond quickly to maintenance needs.

  • Dependable, organized, and comfortable working independently or as part of a team.

  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.

  • Successful completion of background screening and drug testing requirements.

At Prime Independent Living, we're creating communities where older adults can live well, live fully, and enjoy meaningful experiences every day. Our team members play a vital role in making that vision a reality.

If you're looking for a hands-on opportunity where your work matters, your skills are valued, and you can be part of a team creating something special, we'd love to meet you!

description:

Responsibilities

Responsible for the accurate weighing, checking and mixing of specific chemical compounds for product formulations; the calibrating and monitoring of a variety of mixing machinery and the accurate documenting and maintaining of production logbooks and records. They’re also required to follow all departmental and company SOP’s and maintain accurate and timely record keeping on each formulation batch. They must be able to work with Antineoplastic products and assist in the Nanotechnology department.


Job Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for accurate formulation of all production lots
  • Sets-up, load, operate and monitor all mixing machine equipment for product formulations
  • Responsible to weigh out and mixing exact amounts of chemicals according to specific formulas while monitoring (verifying) product output from mixing equipment operations
  • Calibrate, operate and monitor all formulation-related equipment (such as scales, meters, etc.)
  • Responsible for the operations necessary to adjust pH of product for in-process testing before releasing to production lines
  • Responsible for the operations necessary to adjust Oxygen levels of Oxygen sensitive product before releasing to production
  • Required to understand and support the formulation of batches using both a volumetric and gravimetric processes based on the requirements as specified in the individual batch records
  • Clean and sanitizes all tanks, equipment and chemical containers used in the product formulation process in accordance with current SOP’s and cGMP’s

Requirements

  • High school diploma / GED
  • Experience working in manufacturing related industries

Working Environment / Physical Requirements:

  • Job functions require work in respirators, including half-mask and full forced air breathing apparatus. Work environment is clean but requires special gowning procedures. Position requires work in clean room environments where clean room clothing is required. Work with hazardous materials is required where improper handling and failure to comply with outlined procedure could result in exposure to Antineoplastic/hazardous products and raw materials that could lead to serious illness. All safety requirements will be adhered to and complied with.

The Company’s primary business language is English. The successful candidate must be able to effectively speak, read, write, and understand English to perform the essential functions of the position, including independently understanding policies, procedures, training materials, and workplace communications written in English due to our heavily regulated work environment.

title: Director Clinical Pharmacology
location: Americas, US-PA, King of Prussia, CSL Behring
description:
Director, Clinical Pharmacology


Locations: King of Prussia, PA or Glattbrugg, Switzerland
Work Arrangement: Hybrid – 3 days onsite
Reports To: Senior Director, Clinical Pharmacology Lead


About CSL

CSL’s R&D organization is accelerating innovation to deliver greater impact for patients. Through a project-led structure and a strong focus on collaboration, we are building a future-ready organization that thrives in dynamic biotech ecosystems. Join CSL and become part of an agile team committed to developing innovative therapies that make a meaningful difference for patients around the world.


The Opportunity

CSL is seeking a Director, Clinical Pharmacology to provide clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics expertise across a range of programs within its R&D portfolio. This individual will lead clinical pharmacology strategy, guide pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) assessments, and drive the application of modeling and simulation to support drug development decisions throughout the clinical development lifecycle.


The successful candidate will operate with a high degree of independence, bringing strong scientific expertise, innovative thinking, and a solution-oriented approach to cross-functional collaboration. Working closely with clinical development, research, translational science, biostatistics, and other R&D partners, the Director will ensure the integration of clinical pharmacology strategies into global development plans.


This role will also serve as a key clinical pharmacology representative in regulatory interactions, contributing to submission documents, regulatory responses, and discussions with health authorities to support successful development and registration of therapies.


Main Responsibilities and Accountabilities


  • Clinical Pharmacology Strategy: Lead clinical pharmacology and PK-PD strategies for assigned programs across the R&D portfolio, partnering with pharmacometricians, clinical program directors, clinical scientists, biostatisticians, and other cross-functional colleagues.
  • Clinical Study Design and Oversight: Lead the design of clinical pharmacology studies and relevant protocol sections across all stages of drug development. Provide scientific oversight of study implementation in collaboration with Clinical Development, Clinical Safety, and Clinical Research Operations.
  • Pharmacokinetic and PK-PD Analyses: Plan and implement appropriate pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic analyses, including non-compartmental analysis and other relevant analytical approaches, to inform clinical development decisions.
  • Data Interpretation and Reporting: Lead the review and interpretation of clinical pharmacology study results, ensuring high-quality presentation and documentation in clinical study reports, scientific publications, and related study materials.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Represent clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics on clinical development teams, ensuring alignment across functions and integration of clinical pharmacology strategies into global development plans.
  • Modeling and Simulation: Apply innovative pharmacometric methodologies, including modeling and simulation, to integrate pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, patient characteristics, and disease states. Use these insights to inform dose selection, study design, and development strategies throughout the clinical development lifecycle.
  • Regulatory Strategy and Submissions: Provide clinical pharmacology expertise for protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, regulatory submissions, product labeling, and other regulatory documentation. Lead the development of clinical pharmacology strategies and written responses to health authority questions, and contribute to regulatory meetings and filing activities as needed.
  • Research and Translational Science Support: Partner with Research and Translational Science teams to develop preclinical PK-PD knowledge supporting early clinical development strategies and appropriately incorporate pharmacology and toxicology data into early clinical study design.
  • External Scientific Engagement: Establish and maintain relationships with external scientific experts and key opinion leaders in clinical pharmacology to support scientific exchange and advance development approaches.


Qualifications and Experience

  • PhD or PharmD in Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific discipline.
  • A clinical pharmacology research fellowship is preferred.
  • Minimum of 8 years of relevant industry experience for Director-level candidates with a PhD or PharmD, specifically contributing to clinical pharmacology aspects of clinical drug development.
  • Extensive experience in clinical pharmacology, particularly pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and PK-PD strategy.
  • Experience supporting clinical drug development programs across relevant stages of development.

Technical Expertise

  • Advanced understanding of clinical pharmacology principles, including clinical trial design and conduct.
  • Strong knowledge of pharmacokinetic and PK-PD data analysis, interpretation, and application in drug development.
  • Experience with population pharmacokinetic methodologies and interpretation of related analyses.
  • Understanding of the use of biomarkers to inform clinical development decisions.
  • Demonstrated technical expertise in pharmacometrics methodologies and their practical application, including modeling and simulation.
  • Experience contributing to regulatory submissions, clinical pharmacology documentation, and responses to health authority questions.
  • Ability to integrate clinical and nonclinical data to inform dose selection, study design, and clinical development strategies.

Our Commitment


At CSL, we are committed to developing innovative therapies that improve patients’ lives. Join a collaborative, science-driven R&D organization where your expertise in clinical pharmacology and pharmacometrics will help shape development strategies and advance meaningful medical innovation.


#LI-HYBRID


About CSL Behring

CSL Behring is a global biotherapeutics leader driven by our promise to save lives. Focused on serving patients’ needs by using the latest technologies, we discover, develop and deliver innovative therapies for people living with conditions in the immunology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic, respiratory, and transplant therapeutic areas. We use three strategic scientific platforms of plasma fractionation, recombinant protein technology, and cell and gene therapy to support continued innovation and continually refine ways in which products can address unmet medical needs and help patients lead full lives.


CSL Behring operates one of the world’s largest plasma collection networks, CSL Plasma. Our parent company, CSL, headquartered in Melbourne, Australia, employs 32,000 people, and delivers its lifesaving therapies to people in more than 100 countries.

title: Radiation Control Technician
description:
At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit www.bwxt.com. Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Welcome to BWXT
We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We required a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

Position Overview:
Responsible for performing radiological control activities in support of HPDU production operations at BWXT. This role ensures the safe handling of depleted uranium (DU) by conducting radiological surveys, monitoring personnel and work areas, and implementing contamination and exposure controls. The position works closely with operations, safety, and engineering teams to maintain compliance with regulatory requirements and support a strong radiological safety culture.

Location:

On-site in Jonesborough, Tennessee

Your Day to Day as a HPDU Radiation Control Technician:

  • Performs routine and special radiological surveys, including contamination, radiation, and airborne radioactivity monitoring.
  • Collects and analyzes air samples and smears to assess radiological conditions.
  • Implements and maintains contamination control measures to prevent the spread of radioactive materials.
  • Establishes and monitors radiological control boundaries, postings, and access controls.
  • Supports personnel dosimetry programs, including issuance, tracking, and collection of dosimeters.
  • Performs personnel contamination surveys and ensure proper decontamination when necessary.
  • Provides radiological coverage for operations, maintenance, and waste handling activities involving DU.
  • Ensures work is performed in accordance with Radiological Work Permits (RWPs) and applicable procedures.
  • Ensures compliance with applicable TDEC, OSHA, and site-specific radiological safety requirements.
  • Maintains accurate records of radiological surveys, monitoring data, and personnel exposure.
  • Operates, maintains, and performs source checks on radiological monitoring instruments.
  • Identifies and reports instrument malfunctions or calibration issues.
  • Responds to radiological alarms, abnormal conditions, or contamination events.
  • Supports investigation and documentation of radiological incidents or near misses.
  • Assists in training personnel on radiological safety practices, procedures, and requirements.
  • Reinforces proper radiological controls and safe work practices in the field.
  • Promotes a strong radiological safety culture by adhering to ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) principles.
  • Actively participates in safety meetings, briefings, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Required Qualifications:

  • Associate degree in Health Physics, Radiation Protection, or a related field;
  • OR equivalent experience in industrial or chemical environment.
  • Must be able to work any shift.
  • Knowledge of radiological protection principles, contamination control, and monitoring techniques.
  • Experience with radiological instrumentation and survey methods.
  • Ability to interpret procedures, regulations, and technical guidance.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to safety.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and radiological data systems.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) clearance.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Relevant certifications (e.g., NRRPT) are preferred.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.
  • Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.
  • Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.
  • An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.
  • The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.
  • Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

title: Director, Engineering Enrichment Operations
description:
At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit . Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Welcome to BWXT
We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We require a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

Position Overview: Director of Engineering – Enrichment Operations

As the Director of Engineering for BWXT Enrichment Operations, you will lead the full engineering function responsible for delivering a production‑ready centrifuge product and a high‑precision, highly automated factory capability. You will oversee engineering strategy from early concept through prototype/pilot phases to full‑rate production, establishing core systems engineering and systems integration practices to ensure disciplined requirements management, interface control, verification/validation, and seamless subsystem integration. This role is pivotal in standing up a modern digital factory, enabling high‑volume production with aerospace‑grade quality and nuclear regulatory rigor.

Location

On-site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee

Your Day-to-Day as the Director of Engineering

Engineering Leadership & Organization
• Build, scale, and lead a multidisciplinary engineering organization spanning manufacturing, process, facilities, automation, industrialization, and precision systems.
• Serve as the technical authority for manufacturability, scalability, risk management, and readiness.

Systems Engineering (SE)
• Establish a modern systems engineering capability that includes requirements management, architecture development, interface control (ICDs), configuration management, verification and validation, and model-based systems engineering/digital thread practices.
• Define “Definition of Done” at each development gate and ensure complete, build-ready Product Readiness Packs (e.g., BOMs, routers, test plans).

Systems Integration (SI)
• Lead end‑to‑end integration of subsystems into the centrifuge product and supporting systems.
• Develop integration plans, lab capabilities, fixtures, and test regimes to validate subsystem and system-level performance.
• Collaborate with the CTO and ORNL Design Authority to align qualification evidence and change packages; support seamless integration with CMDF pilot builds and transfer to CMF industrialization.

Factory Design, Construction & Startup
• Lead design, build, and commissioning of a high‑precision manufacturing facility.
• Integrate automation, robotics, and digital factory systems to enable high throughput, traceability, and tightly controlled processes.

Manufacturing Excellence & DFx
• Deliver engineering solutions capable of automotive‑pace production with aerospace‑grade quality.
• Drive design for manufacturability, assembly, quality, cost, and industrialization (DFM/DFA/DFQ/DFC).

Quality, Safety & Compliance
• Ensure all engineering designs and processes meet nuclear regulatory, DOE, safety, and BWXT quality requirements.
• Embed compliance gates, audit readiness, and pre‑release checks throughout development.

Program Controls & Schedule
• Partner with Business Operations and Program Controls to maintain a resource‑loaded critical path schedule.
• Support earned value management (EVM) discipline and weekly KPI reviews (SPI/CPI, cost variance, schedule adherence).

Supply Chain & Technical Readiness
• Define technical acceptance criteria for supplier parts, processes, tooling, and special manufacturing steps.
• Support supplier onboarding speed, delivery performance, and technical readiness to protect schedule-critical components.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Work closely with CMDF (prototype/pilot operations), CMF (full-rate industrialization), the CTO/Technology organization, and Operations.
• Drive the transition from low‑rate initial production (LRIP) to full‑rate production (FRP) on cost and schedule.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (advanced degree preferred).
• Fifteen (15+) years of progressive engineering leadership in high‑precision, highly regulated manufacturing environments (nuclear, aerospace, defense, automotive, semiconductor, or similar).
• Demonstrated experience designing, building, commissioning, and scaling a high‑precision manufacturing facility to high‑volume production.
• Strong expertise in advanced manufacturing, automation, precision machining, assembly, metrology, and inspection systems.
• Must be a U.S. citizen capable of obtaining and maintaining a DOE Q clearance; active clearance preferred.
• Proven ability to lead large, multidisciplinary engineering teams in a fast-paced, highly technical environment.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with automotive‑scale manufacturing and assembly; Lean/Six Sigma leadership.
• Hands-on experience deploying Industry 4.0, digital thread, digital twin, and smart factory systems.
• Experience guiding organizations from prototype/pilot phases to high‑rate production in startup‑like or greenfield environments.

What We Offer

• Competitive compensation and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.
• Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance (as applicable).
• Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs, leadership training, and support for continuing education.
• An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates diverse perspectives and enables collaboration across all generations.
• The opportunity to shape a mission‑driven organization advancing the future of energy and national security.
• Continuous learning and development opportunities to support long‑term career growth.

The function encompasses Controls Office, Operational Resilience, Protective Security, Business Continuity and Incident Management.

The Role:

In this role you will support the UAE & MENAT Operational Resilience Lead in transitioning the UAE Operational Resilience programme from delivery into Business as Usual (BAU), strengthening the resilience framework across the region, and driving consistent execution of key activities including entity self-assessment, gap remediation, vulnerability management, and governance and reporting. The role will also support completion and BAU monitoring of Important Business Services (IBS) and enable effective engagement with Business Service Owners (BSOs).

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the transition of the UAE Operational Resilience programme into BAU, helping embed the Operating Model and coordinating the timely completion of annual refresh activities.
  • Support the Operational Resilience Lead in driving engagement and delivery of BSO responsibilities under the operational resilience programme.
  • Provide coordination and secretariat support for the Business Service Owner (BSO) Forum, including agenda planning, materials, actions, follow-ups, and collating the production of BAU packs and reports for lead review and sign-off.
  • Help drive BSO engagement and delivery, tracking ownership, milestones and evidence against responsibilities under the operational resilience programme.
  • Act as a key point of contact with Operational Resilience programme teams, supporting interlocks and day-to-day coordination to progress change implementation activities.
  • Promote Operational Resilience ways of working across the entity, partnering with lines of business, global functions and Technology teams to support monitoring, reporting and performance management for important business services.
  • Track closure of gaps identified through QA by Operational Resilience Lead and maintain transparent status reporting and follow-ups with accountable owners.
  • Work closely with UAE & MENAT stakeholders across businesses, functions and Technology to gather inputs, validate evidence, and support timely delivery.
  • Provide day-to-day risk and control support for IBS vulnerabilities, helping issues data collection, document impacts, and track remediation actions and evidence with the BSOs.
  • Support the Operational Resilience Lead by gathering and analysing MI, incident logs, audit findings, KRIs/KPIs and regulatory updates to identify emerging issues and areas of concern across UAE & MENAT. Track actions and outcomes, maintain issue logs and status dashboards, and escalate material changes promptly to support timely leadership decisions.

In order to apply for this role, you will have the following:

  • A full-time graduation degree of at least three years is essential for obtaining a UAE visa and work permit. For degrees obtained outside the UAE, valid attestations and equivalency are also mandatory.
  • 1- 3 years’ experience in operational resilience, business continuity, operational risk, controls, incident management, or a closely related risk/resilience discipline within a regulated financial services environment is desirable.
  • Experience coordinating governance activities (e.g., forums/committees), including agenda planning, minutes/actions tracking, and production of management packs.
  • Excellent Communication skills to be able to work with multiple stakeholders (Business, Functions, Technology) to drive delivery against agreed milestones, including evidence collection and follow-ups.
  • Planning and organisation: able to structure work, manage competing priorities, and deliver to fixed timelines (e.g., annual refresh cycles).
  • Communication: strong written and verbal skills; able to tailor messages for senior stakeholders and operational teams; able to produce concise, accurate packs.
  • Stakeholder management: confident engaging Business Service Owners (BSOs) and accountable owners to secure actions, evidence, and timely closure of gaps.
  • Analytical capability: able to gather, validate, and interpret MI (incidents, audit findings, KRIs/KPIs) to identify themes, emerging risks, and required actions.
  • Attention to detail: consistently high-quality outputs with minimal errors; strong document and evidence discipline.

title: Managed File Operations Lead
description:
At BBH, Partnership is more than a form of ownership—it’s our approach to business and relationships. We know that supporting your professional and personal goals is the best way to help our clients and advance our business. We take that responsibility seriously. With a 200-year legacy and a shared passion for what’s next, this is the right place to build a fulfilling career.

The Momentum Lead is responsible for leading the global Momentum Operations team and ensuring stability, reliability, security, governance, and continuous improvement of the Momentum Managed File Transfer platform and related services. The role oversees platform monitoring, production support, incident management, client onboarding, Momentum profile builds, change implementation, disaster recovery testing, and service delivery governance.


The Operations Lead serves as the primary leader for operational excellence and platform stewardship across the Momentum environment. This individual drives accountability, ownership, process standardization, technical discipline, and service quality while partnering closely with Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, Risk, Compliance, vendors, clients, and business stakeholders.

This role combines technical operations leadership, people management, strategic planning, risk management, and client service oversight. The successful candidate must protect the production environment, enforce established controls, and have the authority and confidence to challenge, delay, or reject requests that introduce unnecessary risk or do not meet testing, security, operational, or supportability requirements.


Principal Responsibilities


Leadership and Resource Management

· Lead and manage the global Momentum Operations team responsible for production support, platform administration, client onboarding, and profile build activities.

· Establish clear performance objectives and conduct regular performance discussions and annual reviews.

· Develop staffing models, technical coverage, and support rotations appropriate for a mission-critical, 24x7 service.

· Build a culture of accountability, ownership, collaboration, engineering respect, procedural discipline, and continuous improvement.

· Ensure the team has the documentation, training, and technical understanding required to support Momentum safely and consistently.


Service Delivery and Operational Management

· Own the operational support model for Momentum and ensure all issues have clear ownership, status tracking, escalation paths, and resolution plans.

· Provide leadership during production incidents and major service disruptions.

· Coordinate cross-functional response activities across Operations, Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, Risk, Compliance, and external vendors.

· Ensure achievement of service objectives and delivery commitments without compromising platform controls, stability, or client data protection.

· Monitor platform health, operational measures, service trends, capacity, and recurring issues to proactively identify risks and improvement opportunities.

· Drive improvements that increase platform stability, reliability, recoverability, efficiency, and long-term supportability.

· Define, develop, and monitor meaningful measures for operational effectiveness, risk, control adherence, incident trends, profile build quality, and service stability.

· Use ServiceNow, reporting tools, dashboards, and operational data to identify trends, recurring failures, control gaps, and improvement opportunities.

· Track incomplete testing, failed changes, recurring incidents, overdue corrective actions, control exceptions, and undocumented manual processes to closure.


Incident, Problem, and Change Management

· Oversee incident response, root cause analysis, corrective actions, and problem management activities.

· Govern production implementations, maintenance activities, configuration changes, system upgrades, and platform releases.

· Ensure testing, validation, implementation planning, rollback procedures, technical review, and risk assessments are completed before production changes.

· Ensure all changes are tested in the appropriate non-production environment before production implementation. Production must not be used as a testing environment.

· Reject or delay changes that do not meet operational, engineering, security, compliance, testing, or supportability standards.

· Prevent unvalidated manual workarounds, unsupported processes, or control bypasses from becoming accepted production practices.

· Partner with Engineering to improve platform resiliency, reduce recurring incidents, and address technical debt.


Momentum Profile Build and Client Onboarding Governance

· Own the operational governance and review process for Momentum profile build and client onboarding requests.

· Review profile configurations, file routing, endpoints, directories, naming standards, schedules, dependencies, encryption requirements, certificates, transmission protocols, file processing logic, and support procedures.

· Confirm each request includes complete business and technical requirements, accountable ownership, appropriate approvals, test evidence, implementation instructions, rollback steps, and production support documentation.

· Assess requests for consistency with established platform standards, security requirements, operational controls, resiliency expectations, and long-term supportability.

· Challenge custom designs, direct production file placement, manual intervention, control exceptions, or one-off solutions that create avoidable risk.

· Ensure profile builds are repeatable, documented, traceable, and capable of being supported by the global Operations team.

· Maintain clear separation of duties and appropriate review and approval controls throughout the build and implementation process.


Client Service and Stakeholder Management

· Serve as a senior escalation point for business partners and clients.

· Drive timely and effective issue resolution while maintaining technical, risk, and control standards.

· Lead clear communications during incidents, maintenance activities, production changes, and major operational events.

· Develop strong relationships across Technology, Operations, Risk, Compliance, vendors, clients, and business units.

· Provide constructive challenges when proposed timelines or solutions place production stability, client data, or operational integrity at risk.

· Clearly explain decisions, risks, required controls, and remediation actions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Platform Governance and Risk Management

· Act as a steward of the Momentum environment, with responsibility for protecting production stability, client data, service integrity, and platform supportability.

· Ensure adherence to approved procedures, engineering standards, security requirements, change controls, and compliance obligations.

· Establish a risk-first operating culture where stability, security, resiliency, recoverability, and control effectiveness take precedence over convenience or delivery pressure.

· Maintain controls supporting regulatory, audit, access management, and data protection obligations.

· Oversee platform access controls, privileged activity, operational governance, and periodic access reviews.

· Support and govern Business Continuity Planning and Disaster Recovery testing, including documented results and follow-up actions.

· Identify operational and technical risks early, assign accountable owners, track mitigation plans, and escalate unresolved concerns.


Technical Leadership and Engineering Partnership

· Maintain sufficient technical depth to understand Momentum architecture, configurations, integrations, transmission workflows, dependencies, and failure points.

· Review technical designs and implementation plans from an operational, security, resiliency, and supportability perspective.

· Effectively challenge Engineering, Infrastructure, vendors, project teams, and clients when designs conflict with established standards or introduce unnecessary risk.

· Partner with technical teams on capacity planning, monitoring, certificate management, encryption, secure transmission methods, patching, upgrades, and platform modernization.

· Ensure engineering decisions and operational procedures are documented and understood before ownership is transferred to Operations.

· Promote automation and standardization while ensuring controls and human review remain appropriate to the level of risk.


Strategic Planning and Continuous Improvement

· Develop operational roadmaps aligned with business, risk, and technology objectives.

· Identify opportunities for automation, monitoring improvements, process optimization, and reduction of manual activity.

· Lead initiatives that improve service delivery, scalability, resiliency, and supportability.

· Drive operational maturity through documentation, knowledge management, training, standards, and team enablement.

· Support platform modernization and future-state architecture while ensuring operational readiness and controlled implementation.


Required Qualifications


Education

· Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, Management Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.


Experience

· 8+ years of experience in technology operations, production support, infrastructure operations, managed file transfer, or platform management.

· 5+ years of leadership and management experience.

· Experience managing mission-critical production platforms within a financial services or similarly controlled environment.

· Experience leading global operations teams and supporting 24x7 service models.

· Demonstrated experience with incident management, root cause analysis, problem management, change control, service delivery, and operational risk.

· Demonstrated experience reviewing technical implementations and enforcing production readiness standards.

· Experience establishing governance for client onboarding, configuration management, or repeatable technical build processes.


Preferred Qualifications


· Hands-on leadership experience supporting Managed File Transfer platforms, preferably Momentum.

· Experience with SFTP, secure file transmission, encryption, certificate management, endpoint configuration, network connectivity, and secure data exchange services.

· Understanding file routing, scheduling, dependencies, naming standards, automation, monitoring, and operational recovery.

· Experience with ServiceNow and established incident, problem, change, request, and configuration management practices.

· Knowledge of business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience, security controls, and audit requirements.

· Experience working closely with infrastructure, software engineering, network, database, security, risk, and compliance teams.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


· Strong leadership, judgment, and team development skills.

· Strong technical curiosity and the ability to understand complex systems, dependencies, and operational consequences.

· Excellent written, verbal, client, and executive communication skills.

· Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving abilities.

· Ability to manage competing priorities without lowering control or testing standards.

· Strong client service orientation balanced with sound engineering judgment and operational discipline.

· Deep respect for policy, procedure, change control, security, and production governance.

· Ability to identify risk, ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions, and stand firm when operational integrity is at risk.

· Ability to lead through ambiguity and influence across organizational boundaries.

· Ability to translate technical and operational risks into clear business impacts and decisions.

· Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, reporting tools, operational dashboards, and service management platforms.

Salary Range

Boston: $130,000-$180,000 + Annual Target Bonus

Jersey City: $140,000-$190,000 + Annual Target Bonus

title: Consultant, Dealer Changeover  (18- Month Contract)
description:
What you’ll do


"Dealer Mobility" is one of the key concepts in our organization as it provides each Owner/Operator (“Associate Dealer”) of our Canadian Tire Retail Stores, the opportunity to progress into different stores across the country according to their ability and desires. This is accomplished via the Dealer Changeover process.


This process provides for the orderly and equitable sale of a Canadian Tire Store's inventory and assets, along with the transfer of the business operations, from the outgoing Associate Dealer to the incoming Associate Dealer. Ensuring consistency, accuracy, and impartiality is the cornerstone of the Changeover process throughout our network of stores.

The Dealer Changeover Consultant is responsible for planning and consulting on matters of the policy and procedures, ensuring that the entire Changeover process meets the highest standards of accuracy and fairness. The role ensures that all parties understand and accept their respective responsibilities. We are seeking a highly motivated individual to join our field team, requiring extensive travel to support the Changeover process in our Canadian Tire Retail Stores across the country.


  • Plan, facilitate, and support the Associate Dealers and their store staff in preparation for the Changeover process, to maximize the level of accuracy and efficiency in the evaluation of inventory and fixed assets.
  • Demonstrate a strong understanding of asset management and the ability to validate and ascertain the appropriate depreciation category.
  • Ensure the integrity of the inventory count by providing guidance to the store staff using procedures designed to produce the highest level of accuracy possible.
  • Provide coaching to ensure that both the Incoming Associate Dealer and Outgoing Associate Dealer, store staff, and designated third parties comply with the processes and practices as outlined in the Changeover Policy.
  • Develop a store-specific critical path (e.g., actions, people and timeline) for all aspects of the changeover process and work with others to actively problem solve.
  • Prepare financial documentation related to assets to inform the transaction and finalization process.
  • Work collaboratively to continuously identify and implement process improvements required to increase efficiency, consistency, accuracy, and quality of work.

What you bring


  • Ability to travel throughout the country on a weekly/bi-weekly basis, for a maximum of 40 weeks per year.
  • Post-secondary education in business, accounting, or a related field of study is an asset.
  • Strong preference for candidates with 3+ years of retail management experience. Canadian Tire store experience is an asset.
  • Bilingual in French and English (spoken and written) is an asset not required.
  • Demonstrated critical thinking, curiosity, influencing, and conflict resolution skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to organize both time and information.
  • Effective communication skills with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Outlook, and SharePoint.
  • Ability to work autonomously and as part of a field team.

To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

The Strategic Sourcing Buyer is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies that support business growth, supply continuity, supplier diversification, and cost competitiveness. This role focuses on long-term procurement initiatives including supplier development, contract negotiations, new supplier onboarding, risk mitigation, and new product sourcing. The position partners closely with Operations, Engineering, and Corporate Sourcing to build a scalable and resilient supply base while operational buyers manage day-to-day purchasing activities.


Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute sourcing strategies aligned with business growth, new site expansion, and operational requirements.
  • Identify, evaluate, and onboard new suppliers to support capacity, cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
  • Lead RFQ, RFP, and supplier selection activities, including commercial negotiations and contract development.
  • Implement dual-source and supplier risk mitigation strategies to improve supply chain resilience.
  • Support new product introductions and Engineer-to-Order projects through strategic supplier engagement.
  • Negotiate long-term supply agreements and strategic partnerships.
  • Drive cost reduction and value engineering initiatives through supplier collaboration and market analysis.
  • Coordinate sourcing activities with Corporate Sourcing to leverage enterprise agreements and supplier strategies.
  • Monitor supplier market trends, capabilities, and risks to proactively support business objectives.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related field.
  • Minimum of four (4) years of experience in procurement, strategic sourcing, supply chain, or purchasing roles.
  • Demonstrated experience managing supplier relationships, sourcing components, materials, or services, and supporting cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
  • Strong analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and business systems used for procurement and supply chain management.

Preferred Qualifications

  • One (1) or more years of experience leading sourcing initiatives, supplier negotiations, cost-reduction projects, or supplier development programs.
  • Experience working in a manufacturing environment, preferably supporting electrical, industrial, or engineered products.
  • ERP/MRP system experience, with SAP preferred.
  • Familiarity with supplier performance management, contract negotiations, RFQ/RFP processes, and total cost of ownership methodologies.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Finance teams.

Success Measures

  • Cost savings and cost avoidance
  • Supplier risk reduction
  • New supplier qualification and onboarding
  • Dual-source implementation
  • Contract coverage and compliance
  • New product sourcing readiness
  • Supplier performance improvements

Benefits

About Regal Rexnord

Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.


The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.


Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. title: Operations Graduate
description:
About us

Domo Tactical Communications (DTC), part of the Codan Group, is a fast-growing global high-technology company delivering mission-critical wireless communications and broadcast solutions for the most demanding of environments.

DTC develops leading-edge tactical communications technologies, including its revolutionary MeshUltra™ waveform, providing world-class mesh networking, robust wireless products and IP-centric network devices for mission critical applications.

Our passion for innovation keeps us one step ahead in the rapidly changing and increasingly challenging environments within which we perform - whether enforcing the law on the streets of our cities, controlling unmanned vehicles or televising the world's largest sporting events.

What will you be doing?

Within your graduate role, you will be rotated through placements within the various functional teams that, together, ensure the delivery of DTC products to our customers. You will work with the function leaders to promote and drive business process improvements within the various disciplines enabling you to gain full exposure within a fast paced and dynamic environment.

Rotations in support of this could include purchasing, strategic procurement, planning, manufacturing, manufacturing engineering, technical support, project management, test engineering, design engineering, sales and marketing. Throughout these rotations, you may also have the opportunity to lead small project teams, helping you to develop leadership skills and broaden your understanding of the business.

The work undertaken will be tailored to meet your personal development objectives alongside the needs of the business. This approach will provide graduates with a supportive platform to learn, grow and build practical experience within the organisation. With a longer-term focus, graduates will develop the skills, confidence and commercial awareness needed to become valued team members who can contribute meaningfully within a dedicated functional role, while also gaining insight into the wider business and how different teams work together.

What are we looking for:

DTC are looking for a motivated, enthusiastic and highly capable graduate to work within our team.

Requirements:

We are looking for someone who can display many of the following attributes:

  • Analytical mindset
  • Strong problem solving skills
  • Adaptability
  • Agile learner
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Good work ethic

Qualifications:

  • Minimum of a 2:1 Bachelor’s degree (predicted) in Science, Engineering, Mathematics or a related discipline
  • Must have at least 2 A levels at grade B or above in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics related subjects.

The successful candidate must have the right to work in the UK and be eligible for UK Security Clearance.

Anticipated start date: September 2027

Benefits and Culture

At DTC we value our employees.

Benefits include:

  • A personal approach to training and development
  • 25 days annual leave plus Bank holidays
  • Competitive salary
  • A generous pension plan, company match up to 9%.
  • Company bonus scheme
  • Flexible core working hours.
  • Open plan, modern office environment
  • Onsite subsidised café
  • Social events
  • Free onsite parking

Enjoy working as part of a global organisation with teams in Whiteley, Hampshire; USA; Denmark, Singapore; Dubai and Australia.

DTC is committed to promoting a culture that supports personal development and embraces a diverse mix of employees throughout all levels of the organisation.

Interested in a career with us?

Be a part of a growing organisation that drives innovation and excellence, values employees and takes a tailored approach to training and development - if you want to make a difference at DTC, we want to hear from you.

Simply click on APPLY and we will be in contact. Applications will remain open until 6th December 2026.

title: Regional Head of Product Management, GTS
location: Central, Hong Kong Island, Hong Kong
description:
Some careers have more impact than others.

If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be. Whether you want a career that could take you to the top, or simply take you in an exciting new direction, HSBC offers opportunities, support and rewards that will take you further.

Trade has been the foundation of HSBC since 1865, it is evolving fast and so are we. With our network, expertise, and solutions we’re placed to help clients make sense of emerging trends, risks, and opportunities by being the global connectors, innovative problem solvers and strategic partners.



We connect the world through trade. Our footprint gives clients access to roughly 90% of world trade flows providing a powerful mix of local, regional, and global knowledge to help them spot new growth opportunities. We are innovative problem solvers that provide a safer, smoother digital trade experience. We solve business challenges through growth, disruption, or uncertainty, and we bring clients insights and ideas to enable grow and protect their business.



Our comprehensive suite of products and services can be combined into global solutions that help make it easier for businesses to manage trade risk, process trade transactions, and fund trade activities.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Regional Head of Product Management, GTS.

Ready to shape trade finance product strategy across Asia-Pacific?

Why HSBC

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world. Guided by our purpose of opening up a world of opportunity, our ambition is to become the world’s most trusted bank globally, putting customers at the heart of everything we do.

The Role

As Regional Head of Product Management for Global Trade Solutions (GTS) in Asia-Pacific you’ll define and execute the regional strategy across GTS products and propositions. This role matters because ASP is HSBC’s largest region by revenues and plays a central part in strengthening market relevance in trade finance while managing risk and improving client outcomes. You’ll set priorities across product development, technology investment and commercialisation to deliver revenue, cost and profitability outcomes. Working across a complex global matrix you’ll align global consistency and reuse with country-specific client needs plus regulatory and operating requirements. Success looks like stronger product economics, improved digital adoption and automation, and a consistent end-to-end client experience that supports growth. You’ll also strengthen governance and controls so products operate within risk appetite and meet regulatory expectations.

What you'll be doing

  • Set and execute the ASP product strategy across the GTS portfolio in line with strategic priorities
  • Shape the regional suite of products to meet target client needs across markets and segments
  • Optimise product economics through pricing to market, cost discipline and efficient capital consumption
  • Govern product risk by embedding effective controls and ensuring activity operates within risk appetite
  • Oversee product delivery and servicing models to improve client journeys, STP and SUT outcomes
  • Create investment cases and prioritise product and technology enhancements within allocated budgets
  • Deliver development and enhancement initiatives to requirements within agreed timeframes and budgets
  • Commercialise new and existing products through sales tools, training, marketing materials and clear frontline ownership
  • Partner with Sales and frontline teams on client engagement, deal structuring and review of DACs or EAs requiring exceptional approval
  • Manage engagement with third parties and vendors delivering components of GTS products and propositions

What we're looking for

  • Bring extensive knowledge of GTS including traditional trade products, structured trade products and market dynamics
  • Demonstrate substantial senior management experience within GTS across multiple regions and geographies
  • Show strong digital acumen with experience building digital propositions and scaling adoption
  • Apply commercial judgement to pricing, profitability and investment prioritisation across a product portfolio
  • Navigate complex global matrix environments across Product, Digital Channels, Technology, Operations, Risk, Compliance and Finance
  • Manage large complex teams across multiple locations including building capability and ways of working
  • Communicate clearly and influence senior stakeholders through concise narratives and presentations
  • Interpret evolving regulatory requirements and translate them into product design, governance and control expectations

Building the future of trade

If you want to shape how HSBC delivers trade finance across Asia-Pacific this role offers the scope to influence strategy, investment and client outcomes at scale. You’ll work across a diverse footprint, balancing global consistency with the requirements of local markets and regulators. The focus is on creating economically sound propositions, improving digital journeys and strengthening automation and operational effectiveness. Apply to help set the direction for products that support clients to manage working capital, risk and growth across borders.

Opening up a world of opportunity

HSBC is committed to building a culture where all employees are valued, respected and opinions count. We take pride in providing a workplace that fosters continuous professional development, flexible working and opportunities to grow within an inclusive and diverse environment. Personal data held by the Bank relating to employment applications will be used in accordance with our Privacy Statement, which is available on our website.

Issued by The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited.

title: Inspector I (12-Hour Day Shift)
description:

Responsible for visually inspecting filled product off the filling line following Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and current Good Manufacturing Processes (cGMP).   • Performs and documents critical start-up procedures for filling operation such as filter integrity test, line clearance, component verification, etc.
  • Performs and documents quality checks on product.

  • Loads and unloads vials from turntables. Stacks, wraps and moves pallets of product.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • High School graduate or equivalent.
  • One (1) to three (3) years pharmaceutical experience preferred.
  • Basic math skills to perform required calculations (multiplication/division).

The Company’s primary business language is English. The successful candidate must be able to effectively speak, read, write, and understand English to perform the essential functions of the position, including independently understanding policies, procedures, training materials, and workplace communications written in English due to our heavily regulated work environment.

You will work with the QA team, the plant leadership team, and employees at the plant.

Site to add

title: Order Puller, 1st Shift
description:
To thrive as an Order Puller, you must be physically able to lift between 40 and 75 lbs, repeatedly, all day. The job is not hard to master, but it is physically demanding, and you should be working and lifting safely at all times. Being reliable with our attendance expectations is required, as is a high school diploma. You don’t need any previous experience in paint or warehousing. We’ll teach you everything you need to know, which makes this a perfect starting point to launch your career.

In this role, you’re one of the most critical people in the operation. Each day you will fill orders utilizing a scanner gun. After scanning, you will manually lift the cases or buckets onto pallets and then use a rider jack to deliver the pallets to the loading department. You will work in a safe, timely, and accurate manner to keep our shipping department running smoothly, keep the drivers on schedule, and allow us to get paint into stores that depend on us.

Here’s what we’re looking for from you:

  • Attend training. You won’t be out on the floor pulling orders until you are fully trained. You’ll begin with lots of safety training and other education.
  • Safety. We have a meeting and do stretches at the beginning of each shift to warm up and get ready to safely lift paint all day. You will be required to wear proper safety equipment, including steel toed shoes at all times. We’re very proud of our safety record and want you to be part of that.
  • Heavy lifting. The orders come to you electronically and you will pull cases or buckets of paint and load them by hand onto pallets. Cases weigh about 40 lbs and buckets are 75 lbs.
  • A clean facility. You may have worked in dusty or grimy warehouses before, but we pride ourselves on how clean our facility is. We appreciate your help keeping it clean.
  • Diploma or GED. A high school diploma or GED is required.

Here’s what we offer you:


  • Accrue 15 paid days off your first year plus sick days
  • 401(k) retirement plan with 4% match. Annual retirement profit sharing payments
  • Competitive health plans for individuals and families
  • Check out behr.com/careers to view a comprehensive list of our benefits and perks

Founded in 1947, Behr Paint Company is one of the largest manufacturers of paints, primers, decorative finishes, stains, surface preparation and application products for do-it-yourselfers and professionals in the United States, Canada, Mexico and Chile. The Santa Ana, Calif.-based company and maker of the BEHR®, KILZ®, WHIZZ® and E&J® brands is dedicated to meeting the project needs of DIYers, professionals, architects and designers with an unwavering commitment to quality, innovation and value. At Behr Paint, we strive to have all team members bring their best selves and their unique perspectives every day.

title: Senior Quality Inspector
description:
Firestorm Labs is seeking a meticulous and dependable Senior Quality Inspector to join our growing quality team in San Diego. At Firestorm Labs, we are building the future of distributed, mission-adaptive airpower for the modern warfighter. You will be responsible for independently verifying that incoming material, in-process builds, and finished aircraft conform to drawings, specifications, and workmanship standards.
You will be integrated within one of our Integrated Product Teams (IPTs) supporting the Tempest, Squall, and Hurricane FPV aircraft lines. You will perform receiving, in-process, and final inspections, ensure only conforming product moves forward to Flight Test and our customers, and keep every inspection documented and traceable. You will be reporting to the Senior Manager of Production Operations.
What You'll Do
  • Perform receiving inspection of purchased parts and assemblies against purchase orders, drawings, and certificates of conformance.
  • Perform in-process and Final QC inspection of sub-assemblies and aircraft at defined router checkpoints before release to Flight Test.
  • Verify dimensions, workmanship, wiring, solder joints, connectors, fasteners, torque, and markings using calibrated measuring equipment.
  • Accept handoffs from Manufacturing and Test using the standard handoff log, confirming part number, quantity, MOT, and open items.
  • Complete inspection records and router stamps accurately, maintaining full serial and lot traceability.
  • Identify, tag, and segregate nonconforming material, and initiate NCMRs in Jira with clear defect descriptions and photos.
  • Support MRB activities and verify rework and repair per approved dispositions.
  • Support First Article Inspection (AS9102) and supplier quality activities as directed by Quality Engineering.
  • Ensure inspection tools and gauges are calibrated and used correctly.
  • Share defect trends with the IPT and support root cause and corrective action efforts.
  • Performed other duties as directed
Required Qualifications
  • High school diploma, GED or equivalent education
  • 'U.S. Person' as defined by 22 CFR § 120.62 required due to ITAR regulations, which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (Green Card holders), or protected individuals under asylee or refugee status
  • 5+ years of quality inspection experience in aerospace, defense, UAS, electronics, or precision manufacturing.
  • Experience with calipers, micrometers, height gauges, torque tools, and other standard inspection equipment.
  • Experience reading and interpreting engineering drawings, including basic GD&T, and inspection criteria.
  • Strong attention to detail, objectivity, and disciplined documentation habits.
  • Experience communicating findings clearly and constructively with build and test teams.
Preferred Qualifications
  • IPC-A-610 and/or IPC/WHMA-A-620 certification.
  • Experience working within an AS9100-compliant quality management system.
  • Experience with receiving inspection, First Article Inspection (AS9102), and NCMR/MRB processes.
  • ASQ Certified Quality Inspector (CQI) or Certified Quality Technician (CQT).
  • Experience inspecting composite structures, cable harnesses, or electromechanical assemblies.
  • Familiarity with Jira or an ERP/MES system.
Work Environment
  • The position is working onsite at Headquarters in San Diego, CA.
  • Will be working on the production floor and in the receiving area.
  • Standing, bending, and close visual work, including under magnification, for extended periods; ability to lift up to 30 lbs.
  • Use of required PPE, including safety glasses and ESD protection.
  • Occasional overtime to support customer commitments.
Compensation
  • Hourly Base: $32.00 -$42.00 an hour base, commensurate with experience
  • Equity: Meaningful equity grant in a growth-stage defense technology company
The posted salary range reflects an estimate based on a variety of compensation factors, including but not limited to relevant experience, education, certifications, specialized skills, geographic location, and business needs. Actual compensation may vary, and this range is subject to change as our compensation structure or market conditions evolve.
Who We Are
At Firestorm, we’re on a mission to revolutionize how defense solutions are designed and delivered. Our goal is to empower U.S. ally nations to effectively deter aggressors—regardless of their defense budget—through innovative, cost-efficient technologies. We call this vision “democratized deterrence.” As a VC-backed company at the intersection of defense and Silicon Valley, we’re pioneering the development of mission-adaptable aerial vehicles that put power back into the hands of operators. By prioritizing operator effectiveness, we’re pioneering a new era of aerial vehicle design. We aim to upend the traditional defense procurement model by delivering world-class capabilities at a fraction of the usual cost. Join us at Firestorm as we redefine defense procurement, making cutting-edge technology accessible to all at a fraction of the cost.
Benefits & Perks
Our culture fosters collaboration, respect, and trust, empowering passionate people to do their best work. We offer a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for career growth. In addition to an opportunity to take part in an innovative, collaborative and fast-growing business with a highly motivated and skilled team, we also take pride in taking care of our employees. Here are just a few ways that we show our appreciation:
  • We offer comprehensive medical, dental, and visions plans
  • 401(k) Retirement Savings Plan to invest in your long-term retirement goals
  • Equity grants for new hires
  • Unlimited PTO
  • Extremely generous company holiday calendar, including a holiday hiatus in July, & December.
  • Generous Parental Leave
  • Lifestyle Spending Account
  • FSA
  • DCFSA
  • HSA
  • Hospital Indemnity insurance
  • Critical Illness insurance
  • Accident insurance
  • Basic Life/AD&D, short-term and long-term disability insurance, 100% covered by Firestorm. Plus, the option to purchase additional life insurance for you and your family.
  • Mental Health Resources: We provide free mental health resources 24/7 including therapy and more. Additional work-life services, such as free legal and financial support, are available to you as well.
Export Control Compliance
To conform to U.S. government export control regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and Export Administration Regulations (EAR), you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or otherwise eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State or U.S. Department of Commerce.
Equal Opportunity Statement

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic under federal, state, or local law, including those with a criminal history, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the CA Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance. title: Temporary Hospital Based Patient Advocate
description:
Make a real difference in patients’ lives—join Elevate Patient Financial Solutions as a Temporary Hospital Based Patient Advocate and help guide individuals through their healthcare financial journey. This full-time position is located 100% onsite at a hospital in Harvey Illinois, with a schedule working from Wednesday and Thursday 12:00pm to 9:00pm Friday Saturday and Sunday 1:00pm to 9:00pm.
This is a temporary position anticipated to last between 8-12 weeks.

Bring your passion for helping others and grow with a company that values your impact. In 2024, our Advocates helped over 823,000 patients secure the Medicaid coverage they needed. Elevate’s mission is to make a difference. Are you ready to be the difference?

As a Hospital Based Patient Advocate, you play a vital role in guiding uninsured hospital patients through the complex landscape of medical and disability assistance. This onsite, hospital-based role places you at the heart of patient financial advocacy—meeting individuals face-to-face, right in their hospital rooms, to guide them through the process of identifying eligibility and applying for financial assistance. Your presence and empathy make a real difference during some of life’s most vulnerable moments.

Job Summary

The purpose of this position is to connect uninsured hospital patients to programs that will cover their medical expenses. As a Patient Advocate, you will play a critical role in assisting uninsured hospital patients by evaluating their eligibility for various federal, state, and county medical or disability assistance programs through bed-side visits and in-person interactions. Your primary objective will be to guide patients face-to-face through the application process, ensuring thorough completion and follow-up. This role is crucial in ensuring that uninsured patients are promptly identified and assisted, with the goal of meeting our benchmark that 98% of patients are screened at bedside.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
  • Screen uninsured hospital patients at bedside in an effort to determine if patient is a viable candidate for federal, state, and/or county medical or disability assistance.
  • Complete the appropriate applications and following through until approved.
  • Detailed, accurate and timely documentation in both Elevate PFS and hospital systems on all cases worked.
  • Provide exceptional customer service skills at all times.
  • Maintain assigned work queue of patient accounts.
  • Collaborate in person and through verbal/written correspondence with hospital staff, case managers, social workers, financial counselors.
  • Answer incoming telephone calls, make out-bound calls, and track all paperwork necessary to submit enrollment and renewal for prospective Medicaid patients.
  • Maintain structured and timely contact with the applicant and responsible government agency, by phone whenever possible or as structured via the daily work queue.
  • Assist the applicant with gathering any additional reports or records, meeting appointment dates and times and arrange transportation if warranted.
  • Conduct in-person community visits as needed to acquire documentation.
  • As per established protocols, inform the client in a timely manner of all approvals and denials of coverage.
  • Attend ongoing required training to remain informed about current rules and regulations related to governmental programs, and apply updated knowledge when working with patients and cases.
  • Regular and timely attendance.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or abilities.
  • Some college coursework preferred
  • Prior hospital experience preferred
  • Adaptability when dealing with constantly changing processes, computer systems and government programs
  • Professional experience working with state and federal programs
  • Critical thinking skills
  • Ability to maneuver throughout the hospital and patients’ rooms throughout scheduled work shift.
  • Proficient experience utilizing Microsoft Office Suite with emphasis on Excel and Outlook
  • Effectively communicate both orally and written, to a variety of individuals
  • Ability to multitask to meet performance metrics while functioning in a fast-paced environment.
  • Hospital-Based Patient Advocates are expected to dress in accordance with their respective Client’s Dress Code.
  • Hybrid positions require home internet connections that meet the Company’s upload and download speed criteria. Hybrid employees working from home are expected to comply with Elevate’s Remote Work Policy, including but not limited to working in a private and dedicated workspace where confidential information can be shared in accordance with HIPAA and PHI requirements.
The salary of the finalist selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to, internal equity, experience, education, location, specialty and training. This pay scale is not a promise of a particular wage.
The job description does not constitute an employment agreement between the employer and Employee and is subject to change by the employer as the needs of the employer and requirements of the job change.

A System Modeling & Simulation Engineer 1 designs, develops, validates, and maintains dynamic simulations and infrastructure for rapid assessment, integration, and test of complex systems. Simulation applications range from high-level behavioral simulations for visualization and evaluation of system concepts to high-fidelity real-time simulations and Hardware-in-the-Loop infrastructure to support development, integration, test, and sustainment of systems and software.
