title: Mechanical Assembly - Night Shift
description:
Powell People Solving Tough Problems

As a top player in Switchgear and E-house Manufacturing and field servicing, a career with us will challenge you to solve some very tough problems. You will be rewarded with growth, personal development & industry expertise. At Powell, we provide a comprehensive salary package, RRSP matching, extensive benefits and job training all within a professional & friendly working environment.

Based out of the Electrical Division Edmonton (EDE) location, the Assembler will report to the Manufacturing Supervisor of the Switchgear Assembly department. The Assembler will be responsible for the Assembly of electrical units, switchgear, and other Powell products.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Build and assemble mechanical components for Switchgear units.
  • Assemble Switchgear units as per drawings and instructions.
  • Repair identified discrepancies with Switchgear units.
  • Promote a safety culture as well as attend all safety meetings.
  • Ensures quality by following standard work instructions and identifying any potential risks to product quality.
  • Ensure that work areas remain clean and well organized.
  • Other duties as required.

Job Requirements - Core Competencies

  • Positive attitude.
  • Willingness to learn.
  • Ability to follow direction from Senior Assemblers and Lead Assemblers.
  • Effectively demonstrates on-time delivery and the ability to stay focused on goals and responsibilities.
  • Self-starter with ability to take on multiple tasks with a drive to succeed.
  • Challenges the status quo; looks for better or more efficient ways to get results.
  • Ability to adapt to new ideas, technology, processes or product changes.
  • Believes and displays through actions that our customers represent our current success and remain vital to our future growth.
  • Demonstrates integrity and ethical decision making.
  • Conscientious, thorough, accurate, and reliable when performing and completing job tasks.
  • Able to work effectively within your team and around other departments and their activities.
  • Ability to learn and adhere to all manufacturing policies and practices to ensure adherence to ISO requirements
  • Must have a basic command of the English language, both written and verbal.

Qualifications

  • Minimum education level of a High School Diploma is required.
  • Minimum 0-3 years’ of experience in a manufacturing environment.
  • Previous experience in Switchgear units is considered an asset.
  • Ability to read a tape measure (including conversions from fraction to decimal and conversely from decimal to fraction and metric to imperial).
  • Knowledge of machines and tools including their design, use, repair and maintenance.
  • Basic computer knowledge considered and asset.
  • Prior ability or interest in building or repairing mechanical components considered an asset.
  • Safety training certificates are an asset for the position.

Work Authorization: This is a permanent position. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada at the time of hire. Immigration sponsorship is not typically available and will be considered only where supported by business needs and applicable legal requirements.

Working Conditions

  • Safety sensitive position in a temperature controlled manufacturing or industrial environment with occasional outside activities.
  • Required to wear personnel protective equipment at all times (i.e., hard hats, safety glasses, hearing protection, safety harnesses as required) and respirators when required.
  • Must be able to work from all type of ladders (step ladders, "A" frame ladders and all size extension ladders) and scaffolding.
  • Working at heights usually no higher than 30 feet in the air on or using proper lift equipment.

Physical Requirements

  • Able to maintain body equilibrium and agility to prevent falling when walking, standing, crouching, ascending or descending stairs.
  • Bending the body at the waist, the legs at the knees, and extending arms and hands in any direction in a repetitive manner continuously.
  • Continuous standing, walking 50-300 foot distances for long periods of time with only occasional sitting.
  • Must be able to climb stairs frequently throughout the shift.
  • Able to frequently look over shoulders, work with both arms above shoulders and use both arms at full length frequently.
  • Using upper extremities to apply or exert a force continuously up to 50lbs.
  • Ability to use hand tools such as tin snips, hammer, and power tools (some vibrating), for long periods of time with frequent repetition.

Who we are

Powell Canada Inc. is a subsidiary of Powell Industries, which is located in Houston, Texas. Globally, we have over 70 years of experience. Powell Canada is a reputable electrical manufacturing, valve servicing and electrical/instrumentation contracting company. We hold a strong industry presence with offices located in Acheson, Calgary and Montreal.

Powell strives to create one unified company through training, communication and leadership. We offer diversified services based on our customer’s needs, keeping us on the cutting edge of new products and services within our industry.

Your Partner in Safety

title: Systems Engineer
description:
At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. A U.S.-based company, BWXT is a Fortune 1000 and Defense News Top 100 manufacturing and engineering innovator that provides safe and effective nuclear solutions for global security, clean energy, environmental restoration, nuclear medicine and space exploration. With more than 7,800 employees, BWXT has 14 major operating sites in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. We are the sole manufacturer of naval nuclear reactors for U.S. submarines and aircraft carriers. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. Our joint ventures provide environmental restoration and operations management at a dozen U.S. Department of Energy and NASA facilities. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit . Follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Welcome to BWXT
We believe in empowering our employees and cultivating a dynamic workplace that fosters growth and collaboration. Whether you’re an experienced professional or just starting your career, you'll find opportunities to challenge yourself, learn from seasoned experts, and contribute to nuclear innovation. We required a diverse range of skills to support our work in the markets that drive our business and welcome candidates from all backgrounds and life stages who are passionate about making a difference.

BWXT is People Strong, Innovation Driven - be part of BWXT’s innovation hub. BWXT’s Advanced Technologies (AT) group researches, designs, and develops innovative new nuclear reactors, nuclear rocket propulsion systems, and radioisotope production systems for both internal and external customers.

If you are looking for a career where your experience is valued, innovative thinking is fostered, and barrier-free teamwork is embraced every day, then this opportunity is for you.

Position Overview:

As our Systems Engineer you will provide the high-level systems thinking necessary to bring together the contributions of a cross-disciplinary development team. The primary responsibility is to translate the expectations of customers and other stakeholders into work products, including requirements and operational concepts that guide the development team to a successful solution. This role requires the ability to maintain a top-down high-level view of projects and a multi-disciplined background in relevant technologies.

Location:

On-site in Lynchburg, VA

Your Day to Day as a Systems Engineer:

  • Collaborate with customers, regulators, and program managers to develop top-level requirements which encompass the needs of all stakeholders.
  • Define the design deliverables necessary for successful project execution with a team of engineers of varied disciplines.
  • Perform architectural design and requirement specification for complex systems-of-systems.
  • Collaborate with engineers of varied disciplines to define system interfaces.
  • Understand and mitigate technical risks to ensure project success.

Required Qualifications:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or Physics is required.
  • A minimum of four (4) years of related engineering experience is required.
  • Must have demonstrated ability to conceptualize and define complex systems-of-systems.
  • Must have demonstrated ability to translate customer/client expectations into clear, concise, verifiable requirements.
  • Must have general understanding of Systems Requirements, Architecture, Interface Definition, and Design.
  • Must have demonstrated ability to collaborate on the creation, development, and presentation of technical briefings.
  • Must have demonstrated ability to recognize and solve technical problems.
  • Must be a self-starter, capable of effectively working both as part of a team and independently.
  • Must be familiar with standard MS Office applications.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen.
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) or Department of Defense (DOD) security clearance, whichever is required.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in a STEM discipline.
  • Knowledge of International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE) practices and handbooks.
  • Knowledge of DOORs or other requirements management tools.
  • Knowledge of Model Driven Architecture (MDA) / Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE).
  • Experience or knowledge of nuclear reactors.
  • Experience or knowledge of nuclear propulsion.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive salary and benefits package, including health, dental, and retirement plans.
  • Flexible work schedules and paid time off to promote a healthy work-life balance.
  • Professional development opportunities, including mentorship programs and sponsorship for continuing education.
  • An inclusive atmosphere that celebrates new perspectives and supports collaboration between different generations.
  • The chance to be part of a mission-driven organization making a positive impact on the future of energy.
  • Opportunities for continuous learning and training to grow throughout your career!

title: Electronics Engineering Degree Apprentice
description:
Job Description:


The opportunity


Leonardo offers a range of Apprenticeships from 2-5yrs. across a variety of STEM and business routes, offering paid training, coupled with on the job learning that enables you to gain practical skills, experience and knowledge that sets up the best start to your career. We offer competitive entry salaries and fully support your academic learning through to qualifications, with salary increases as you progress.

We support helping you settle into your new location ensuring you are familiar with the team and have a warm welcome from day 1. There is a member of our Apprentice team at each site, helping you progress, ensuring your study time is protected, enabling access to digital learning as well as opportunities to get involved with the local community and STEM projects, enhance many aspects of each programme.

Programme Description

Looking for a great start to your career in Electronics Engineering, earning and learning on a professionally accredited, award-winning scheme? We are looking to recruit the experts of the future on our nationally recognised, award-winning Apprenticeship Programmes.

You will be working within world class facilities regardless of which site you are based. There may also be opportunities to travel between the Company’s UK sites to meet with colleagues, customers and suppliers.


How this role fits in


Leonardo's four year Electronics Engineering Degree Apprenticeship programme is looking for people who understand the importance of communication, who are able to work well as part of a team and also on their own initiative. You will have the drive and commitment to work through difficult problems to find the right engineering solutions.

Role description

You will study with one of our academic partners for completion of a Level 6 Bachelor Honours Degree (BEng) through a mixture of work based learning and attendance at University. This Apprenticeship aligns with the current edition of the UK Standard for Professional Engineering Competence (UK-SPEC) at Incorporated Engineering (IEng) and Embedded Electronics & System Design standards (ST0151).

We need people who understand the importance of our Customers and are ready to commit to working in the business, whilst also committing to a 4 year degree programme. At the end of the programme, you will work as a highly qualified member of our Electronics Engineering community.

You will be working for a company at the cutting edge of technology, as well as enhancing your skills and business acumen, opening up your horizons to the diverse and dynamic ways to apply your academic learning in a practical environment.

We have created a programme across our UK sites that value those who continuously ask questions and look to resolve problems through creative and innovative thinking.

Who would suit this role?

Leonardo values people that look to always develop throughout their career and along with an eager willingness to learn, a successful apprenticeship with Leonardo involves a drive to deliver results, sometimes from your own initiative, a patience for problem solving, as well as a need to comply with safety instructions and clear process compliance at all times. We view commitment to the programme and learning objectives very highly.

Note: This Apprenticeship assumes the candidate has little professional engineering experience and is NOT suitable for candidates who already have an engineering degree.

Salary £23,500

During your Apprenticeship we encourage you to spend at least 3/4 days a week on site to integrate with your team and maximise your learning experience.

Mandatory

Qualifications

You must have (as a minimum) the following qualifications:

3 x A Levels (A*- C) one of which must be - English, Maths or a technical related subject

OR

An alternative Level 3 qualification, which must be an engineering or ICT related subject

AND

GCSE (Grade 4 - 9 / A*- C) in Maths and English

Security Clearance

At Leonardo, many of our roles are subject to security and export control restrictions set by UK Government Security requirements and customer obligations. As a result, and in line with the UK Government Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS) requirements, all successful applicants will be asked to provide evidence of identity, eligibility to work in the UK, criminal record declaration information and employment and/or education history verification for the previous five years.

For staff operating in more sensitive posts, there is an additional range of personnel security controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV). As part of this process, a range of factors may be considered, including an individual's background, travel history, nationality, previous nationalities held and other information relevant to the vetting assessment.

To be eligible for National Security Vetting at SC level, applicants will generally be expected to have continuously resided in the UK for the previous five years. For DV clearance, this is typically ten years. In some circumstances, time spent overseas may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Additional vetting requirements may apply upon appointment.

For more information and guidance please visit:

Why join us

At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do, key contributors in shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.

We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.

  • Time to recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year.
  • Secure your future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution.

title: Principal Clinical Statistical Programmer (Portfolio Development / Biometrics / Programming)
location: EMEA, GB, Berkshire, Maidenhead, CSL Behring
description:
The Role
CSL is looking for a Principal Programmer to take technical ownership of statistical programming across a compound or programme, not just a single study. You’ll be the person who sets how the programming gets done across multiple trials and through to submission, and the one a study team, a CRO or a regulator’s question ultimately lands with. This is still a hands-on role, and you’ll write and validate code when the work calls for it. Most of your impact, though, comes from the decisions upstream: how standards are applied across studies so an integrated analysis comes together cleanly, how CRO work is scoped and held to account, and how a submission package is built so it holds up under review. You’ll work as a peer to biostatistics, data management, medical writing and regulatory leads, and you’ll be in the room early enough to shape a programme’s analysis strategy rather than inherit it.


Hybrid Based (3 days a week onsite) in Maidenhead


Why It Matters
A single well-programmed study is valuable. A programme where every study was built to the same standard, so pooled safety and efficacy analyses come together without months of rework, is what gets a submission over the line. This role sits at that level. You spot the inconsistency between two studies’ ADaM conventions before it becomes an ISS problem, push back on a CRO deliverable that technically meets spec but won’t survive a reviewer, and make the call on the trade-offs between speed, consistency and regulatory defensibility. When an agency query comes back, you’re the one who knows why the data was built the way it was.


What You’ll Be Responsible For
You’ll lead programming at the programme or compound level, across in-house and outsourced studies, from study setup through integrated analyses and regulatory submission. You’ll set direction for other programmers, internal and external, and help shape how the wider programming function works.

  • Serve as lead programmer for a compound or programme, overseeing programming across multiple clinical trials and ensuring consistency of standards and approach
  • Lead the planning, specification and delivery of integrated analyses (ISS/ISE) and pooled datasets, and own the submission-ready data package, including define.xml, reviewer guides (cSDRG/ADRG) and conformance checks
  • Define programming strategy for outsourced studies, set expectations for CROs and hold their deliverables to submission standard
  • Act as the programming point of contact for regulatory submissions and agency queries, working with biostatistics and regulatory colleagues on responses
  • Lead and mentor other programmers, providing technical direction, review and day-to-day guidance across the programme
  • Contribute to departmental standards, macros, tools and process improvement, including the adoption of new approaches such as R-based workflows
  • Take on hands-on programming and ad hoc analytical work (exploratory analyses, publication support, regulatory responses) as the programme requires

Experience Required

  • Substantial statistical programming experience in pharmaceutical, biotech, CRO or clinical research settings, including lead programmer responsibility across multiple studies
  • Expert SAS proficiency (Base/Macro/Stat/Graph); working experience with R or other languages is a strong plus
  • Deep, practical knowledge of current CDISC standards (CDASH, SDTM, ADaM, define.xml) and how to apply them consistently across a programme
  • Track record of leading integrated analyses (ISS/ISE) and delivering submission-ready data packages
  • Direct experience of supporting regulatory submissions end to end (FDA required; PMDA, NMPA or EMA experience a plus), including responding to agency queries
  • Experience of setting direction for and overseeing CRO and vendor programming work
  • Experience of leading, mentoring or technically directing other programmers
  • BSc in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics or a related field (MSc desirable); equivalent experience and certifications will also be considered

description:
Title: Supply Planner

Location: Kennewick, WA

Job Requisition ID: Req-271986

Time Type: Full time


About Lamb Weston


You’ve probably enjoyed our fries without even knowing it! As a leading manufacturer in our industry, we inspire and bring people together with foods they love and trust. Our customer base includes international food service providers, restaurants, and households in over 100 countries around the world.


A highly innovative global corporation with a start-up mindset, we empower every individual to make a genuine difference. You’ll gain access to hands-on training to fuel your growth and success, explore opportunities for new solutions, and you’ll join a winning team of 10,000+ people all dedicated to raising the bar – together.


If you have a strong drive for results, a desire to help us bring the world together through our fries, and are ready for a fresh challenge, we want to hear from you.

Job Description Summary

The Supply Planner develops and maintains feasible, stable supply and production plans that translate approved demand and supply priorities into executable schedules across assigned plants, lines, or product categories. The role balances capacity, material availability, labor, changeovers, sanitation and maintenance windows, inventory targets, manufacturing efficiency, and customer service requirements. The Supply Planner serves as the execution bridge between supply planning and manufacturing by proactively identifying constraints, evaluating scenarios, recommending tradeoffs, and maintaining disciplined planning parameters and master data to improve plan reliability, execution readiness, and decision quality.

Job Description

Supply Planning & Production Scheduling

  • Develop and maintain supply and production plans across assigned plants, lines, or categories, translating approved supply requirements into executable schedules.
  • Align plans with demand priorities, capacity, material availability, labor, production rates, changeovers, sanitation and maintenance windows, and inventory objectives.
  • Manage plan and schedule stability while responding to demand shifts, supply constraints, and operational disruptions in a timely, fact-based manner.

Execution Risk & Scenario Planning

  • Evaluate supply and schedule risks related to capacity, material shortages, labor constraints, downtime, yield, quality holds, changeovers, sanitation windows, and production sequencing.
  • Build scenarios for production timing, recovery plans, inventory builds, constraint mitigation, and customer impact.
  • Quantify tradeoffs across service, inventory, capacity utilization, manufacturing efficiency, cost, waste, and working capital; escalate material risks with clear options and recommended actions.

Digital Planning & System-Based Decision-Making

  • Use Kinaxis Maestro and other planning tools, dashboards, alerts, scenarios, optimization outputs, and digital workflows to support exception-based supply planning and scheduling.
  • Apply a trust-but-verify mindset to system-generated plans and recommendations by validating assumptions, parameters, constraints, data quality, and operational feasibility.
  • Document override rationale, identify automation opportunities, and partner with the Planning COE, Manufacturing, and technology teams to improve workflows, master data, and adoption.

Cross-Functional Alignment & Decision Support

  • Partner with Manufacturing, Supply Capacity Planning, Materials Planning, Deployment, Procurement, Logistics, Quality, Maintenance, Customer Service, Finance, and Commercial teams.
  • Facilitate alignment on production priorities, schedule feasibility, constraint resolution, recovery actions, and inventory build strategies.
  • Communicate what changed, why it matters, the service and financial implications, and the decision needed while promoting enterprise-first outcomes rather than local optimization.

Planning Parameters, Performance & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain planning and scheduling parameters, including production rates, calendars, frozen windows, changeover rules, sanitation windows, sequencing logic, material constraints, and plant master data.
  • Monitor supply plan and MPS adherence, schedule attainment and stability, production plan adherence, capacity utilization, changeover performance, service risk, and inventory impact.
  • Conduct root cause analysis on recurring misses and exceptions; recommend improvements to planning routines, governance, data quality, handoffs, and constraint ownership.

Scope: (Include scope/ complexity of the role that can be measured and are pertinent to the roles responsibilities)

  • Owns supply and production plans, planning parameters, constraint visibility, and execution readiness for assigned plants, lines, categories, or products.
  • Supports cross-functional decisions affecting customer service, inventory, capacity, manufacturing efficiency, cost, waste, and working capital across short- and mid-term planning horizons.
  • Operates independently within E2E Planning governance, standardized processes, decision rights, and escalation paths.

Basic & Preferred Qualifications

Education/ Certifications: (Required & Preferred)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Business, Engineering, Manufacturing, Logistics, or a related field required. Prior experience may also be considered.
  • APICS CPIM or CSCP certification preferred; Lean, Six Sigma, or project management certification is a plus.

Skills and Experience:

  • 5–8 years of experience in supply planning, production planning, master production scheduling, materials planning, manufacturing operations, or inventory planning.
  • Strong understanding of supply planning, production scheduling, capacity planning, inventory management, constraint management, production sequencing, changeovers, and manufacturing operations.
  • Experience using ERP and advanced planning systems such as SAP ECC, SAP IBP, Kinaxis Maestro, Oracle, Blue Yonder, o9, or equivalent.
  • Experience with Power BI, Tableau, Excel, SQL, or other analytical tools preferred.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to model scenarios, identify root causes, validate constraints, and recommend practical actions.
  • Ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders and communicate supply risks, tradeoffs, business implications, and recommendations clearly.
  • Strong business acumen with understanding of customer service, inventory, cost, capacity utilization, manufacturing efficiency, waste, and working-capital tradeoffs.
  • Demonstrated digital fluency, change agility, data stewardship, planning parameter discipline, and a trust-but-verify mindset toward system-generated plans and recommendations.

  • Some travel may be required (% of time if significant)
  • Most work is performed in a temperature-controlled office environment
  • Incumbent may sit for long periods of time at desk or computer terminal
  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear.
  • Incumbent may use calculators, keyboards, telephone and other office equipment in the course of normal workday
  • Stooping, bending, twisting and reaching may be required in completion of job duties

Industry-Competitive Benefits

Coupled with our compensation and bonus incentive programs, our benefits deliver rewards that are market competitive. Some of the most attractive elements of our benefit programs include:

  • Health Insurance Benefits - Medical, Dental, Vision

  • Flexible Spending Accounts for Health and Dependent Care, and Health Reimbursement Accounts

  • Well-being programs including companywide events and a wellness incentive program

  • Paid Time Off

  • Financial Wellness – Industry leading 401(k) plan with generous company contributions, Financial Planning Services, Employee Stock purchase program, and Health Savings Accounts, Life and Accident insurance

  • Family-Friendly Employee events

  • Employee Assistance Program services – mental health and other concierge type services

Benefits may vary based on location, job role/level, job status, and/or the terms of any applicable collective bargaining agreements.

The anticipated close date is a good faith estimate for when this job will be closed. Some jobs may be unposted or filled earlier or later than the Anticipated Close Date depending on interview processes and business needs.

At BWX Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: BWXT), we are People Strong, Innovation Driven. Our company supplies precision manufactured components, services and fuel for the commercial nuclear power industry across four continents. BWXT’s technology is driving advances in medical radioisotope production in North America and microreactors for various defense and space applications. For more information, visit . Position Overview


The Data Analyst – Project Controls will play a key role in supporting the development, implementation, and sustainment of Earned Value Management (EVM) across the site. This role focuses on building reliable, automated data flows, developing dashboards and reporting tools, and enabling project teams to make informed, data‑driven decisions. The analyst will work closely with the Project Controls Manager, Project Managers, and cross‑functional stakeholders to ensure project information is accurate, accessible, and actionable.

• Develop, maintain, and optimize data pipelines needed for EVM, budget tracking, forecasting, and overall project controls reporting.
• Build and manage Power BI dashboards that provide clear visibility into cost, schedule, performance metrics, and trends for Project Managers and leadership.
• Use advanced Excel and Power Query skills to clean, transform, and consolidate data from multiple sources into consistent reporting structures.
• Support preparation of EACs (Estimates at Completion), load boards, and other project control documents.
• Assist with quoting and cost analysis during Market Basket Quoting efforts
• Present project information directly to Project Managers to help them understand performance drivers, risks, and opportunities without having to mine or manipulate raw data themselves.
• Help design and refine new tools, templates, and automation solutions that make project controls processes more efficient and easier for PMs to adopt and provide the trainings.
• Provide insights, identify anomalies, and help build a consistent data-driven culture within the project teams.

Required Skills & Qualifications


• Proficiency in Power BI report development, including DAX, modeling, and data visualization best practices.
• Strong Excel capabilities, including advanced formulas, pivot tables, Power Query, and data shaping.
• Experience working with project data, financials, or cost/schedule tracking systems.

Preferred Skills & Qualifications


• SQL, DAX, Python, VBA, Advanced Excel Modeling, SAP

title: Head of Productivity Suite Engineering Lead - AI
description:
Ready to evolve HPS from chat to agentic productivity at global scale?

Why HSBC

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organisations in the world. Guided by our purpose of opening up a world of opportunity, our ambition is to become the world’s most trusted bank globally, putting customers at the heart of everything we do.

The Role

This Director level role oversees the engineering organisation for HSBC Productivity Suite (HPS) - a portfolio of AI-enabled productivity solutions used by colleagues across the bank. You’ll own delivery, operational performance and the technical evolution of HPS including the transition from a primarily chat-based solution towards more agentic and autonomous capabilities. The role covers around 50 engineers across the UK, China, India and Poland with around 6-7 team leads reporting directly. Working in partnership with Product and the wider Technology organisation you’ll translate roadmap priorities into secure, scalable and well controlled production outcomes. Success means valuable personal-agent capabilities delivered for colleagues alongside stronger engineering pace, quality and operational performance in a regulated environment.

What you'll be doing

  • Oversee delivery of the HPS engineering roadmap in partnership with Product and wider Technology
  • Steer the transition of HPS towards personal-agent and agentic AI capabilities
  • Set technical direction across applications, AI and Agentic AI, platforms, architecture, data, APIs and developer tooling
  • Deliver secure, scalable, reliable and resilient production systems with strong support, monitoring and incident management
  • Embed engineering practices across design, testing, automation, DevSecOps and observability to improve pace and quality while managing cost
  • Maintain robust technology, privacy, model-risk, cyber, compliance and operational controls
  • Build and sustain an inclusive global engineering organisation across the UK, China, India and Poland including team structure and ways of working
  • Develop technical talent through coaching, role modelling and clear expectations for engineering standards and delivery outcomes
  • Make technology choices that remain relevant as the AI landscape evolves balancing innovation with responsible AI and production standards

What we're looking for

  • Bring substantial hands-on software engineering experience turning concepts into enterprise-grade products
  • Show proven experience delivering and operating large-scale AI-enabled production systems including GenAI applications
  • Demonstrate expertise in LLM-based applications, personal agents, agentic workflows and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
  • Apply practical experience with model evaluation, safety guardrails and responsible AI in production
  • Use hands-on engineering skills across Python, APIs, microservices, databases, cloud platforms, containers and Kubernetes
  • Establish DevSecOps, automated testing, observability and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices for reliable production operations
  • Set architecture, engineering standards and technical direction for complex systems with clear trade-offs and operational accountability
  • Manage delivery across distributed, multi-country engineering teams and partner with Product Owners on roadmaps and measurable outcomes

Building Agentic Productivity at HSBC

HPS is on a clear journey from chat-based assistance to personal-agent capabilities that help colleagues get more done with less friction. This role shapes the engineering direction and delivery that makes that transition real and safe at scale. You’ll work closely with Product to turn priorities into robust production outcomes while strengthening engineering pace, quality and operational performance. If you want to build agentic AI capabilities that are secure, well controlled and genuinely useful for colleagues we’d welcome your application.

Being open to different points of view is important for our business and the communities we serve. At HSBC, we’re dedicated to creating diverse and inclusive workplaces - no matter their gender, ethnicity, disability, religion, sexual orientation, socio-economic background or age. We are committed to removing barriers and ensuring careers at HSBC are inclusive and accessible for everyone to be at their best. We take pride in being a Disability Confident Leader and will offer an interview to people with disabilities, long term conditions or neurodivergent candidates who meet the minimum criteria for the role.

title: PMTS ASIC Digital Design IP ENGINEERING
description:
About GlobalFoundries:

GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com.

Summary of Role:

The PMTS Digital Design Engineer will lead the architecture implementation, microarchitecture development, and RTL design of high-performance processor cores and subsystem components. This role requires deep expertise in processor design, strong technical leadership, and the ability to drive complex SoC development programs from concept through silicon bring-up.

The candidate will work closely with architecture, verification, physical design, DFT, firmware, and software teams to deliver competitive processor products meeting performance, power, area, and schedule targets.

Essential Responsibilities:

Processor Microarchitecture & RTL Design

  • Develop and implement microarchitecture for CPU cores, cache subsystems, memory management units (MMU), interconnects, and system controllers.
  • Translate architectural specifications into high-quality RTL designs using Verilog/SystemVerilog.
  • Define and review detailed design specifications, block-level architectures, and implementation strategies.
  • Drive performance optimization, power reduction, and area-efficient design methodologies.
  • Analyze and resolve complex design trade-offs involving latency, throughput, and scalability.

Technical Leadership

  • Lead critical processor design initiatives across multiple functional blocks.
  • Mentor junior and senior engineers on microarchitecture, RTL coding practices, and design methodologies.
  • Conduct architecture, microarchitecture, and RTL design reviews.
  • Establish design guidelines and best practices across the organization.
  • Influence roadmap and technology decisions for future processor generations.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with architects to evaluate new features and enhancements.
  • Work closely with verification teams to define verification plans and close coverage.
  • Support synthesis, timing closure, low-power implementation, and physical design activities.
  • Collaborate with DFT teams to ensure manufacturability and testability.
  • Support silicon bring-up, debug, characterization, and production ramp activities.

Performance Analysis & Optimization

  • Conduct design performance analysis and bottleneck identification.
  • Drive microarchitectural enhancements to improve IPC, memory latency, and system efficiency.
  • Analyze workload behavior and benchmark performance.
  • Participate in power-performance-area (PPA) optimization efforts.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's or master's degree in electrical engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field.
  • 12+ years of experience in processor, CPU, DSP, or complex SoC digital design.
  • Deep understanding of processor microarchitecture, including:
    • Pipeline design
    • Cache architectures
    • Branch prediction
    • Memory hierarchy
    • MMU/TLB designs
    • Interrupt and exception handling
    • Coherency protocols
  • Expert-level RTL design experience using Verilog/SystemVerilog.
  • Strong understanding of synthesis, timing analysis, CDC, RDC, and low-power design techniques.
  • Experience with industry-standard EDA tools and design flows.
  • Strong debugging and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with RISC-V, ARM, MIPS, ARC, or custom CPU architectures.
  • Knowledge of multi-core and heterogeneous computing systems.
  • Experience in AI/ML acceleration, vector processing, or advanced computing architectures.
  • Experience with performance modeling and architectural simulation.
  • Silicon bring-up and post-silicon debug experience.
  • Exposure to safety-critical designs (ISO 26262, DO-254) is a plus.

title: Clinical Laboratory Technician I
description:
Who We Are & What We Do
At Helix, our mission is simple: to help everyone improve their lives through their DNA.

Ready to make a real-world impact with your skills? At Helix, we're transforming healthcare by making genomics a standard of care. We partner with health systems and life science companies to accelerate the integration of genomic data into clinical practice. Join us in building a future where healthcare is personalized, proactive, and powered by genomics.

The Helix clinical laboratory processes genomic samples at a scale very few labs in the world can match, powering the diagnostic and screening tests that health system partners depend on every day. As a Clinical Laboratory Technician I, you'll be on the floor executing the workflows that make that scale possible: Whole Exome, Whole Genome, and Proteomics assays running in a CLIA-certified, CAP-accredited environment built for high throughput. This is a production role under direct supervision, making it the perfect place to build foundational skills on technology at the leading edge of precision medicine.

As a Clinical Laboratory Technician I, you will:
  • Execute pre-analytical and analytical workflows following established SOPs, spanning from sample handling through assay completion.
  • Maintain accurate, complete documentation in required systems and logs, as reliable records are what keep the lab compliant and results trustworthy.
  • Recognize and escalate deviations (such as instrument flags or specimen discrepancies outside your scope) with enough detail so the right person can resolve the issue quickly.
  • Support QC activities and help uphold the standards that keep our CLIA and CAP certifications in good standing.
  • Coordinate with your team on shift handoffs and daily throughput, contributing directly to quality, TAT, and production KPIs.
  • Share observations about workflow patterns with your lead, since small improvements add up quickly when operating at this volume.
About you:
  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical, Physical, Biological, or Clinical Laboratory Science, or Medical Technology.
  • Hands-on lab experience from industry, internship, or coursework.
  • Working knowledge of molecular biology concepts and common lab techniques, ensuring you can follow an experimental method and understand why each step matters.
  • High attention to detail in a regulated environment to catch discrepancies before they become problems.
  • Clear communicator who surfaces issues with enough context for leadership to take immediate action.
  • Adaptable and tech-forward with an eagerness to learn and work with new technologies, such as AI tools and automated platforms, as our laboratory operations evolve.
  • Available Tuesday–Saturday on first shift (7am–3:30pm) or second shift (2pm–10:30pm), with flexibility for overtime as business needs require.
Pluses:
  • Familiarity with high-throughput or automated laboratory workflows.
  • Prior experience in a CLIA, CAP, or otherwise regulated lab setting.

Expected Interview Process:
1) Recruiter Screen 2) Manager Screen/Tech Screen 3) Onsite 4) Offer

Expected Pay For This Role:
There are 3 distinct parts to your Helix offer: 1) Base Salary 2) Annual Bonus 3) Equity
  • Expected Helix Base: $29/hr - $36/hr
  • Expected Helix Discretionary Annual Bonus: 5% of your annual salary
  • Equity: We offer generous equity at Helix. If you receive a Helix offer your recruiter will book dedicated time with you to educate you on our equity model.

Aside from working alongside brilliant, dedicated, passionate, down-to-earth, curious, warm, and thoughtful people, we also provide great benefits:
  • Comprehensive Health Insurance with Date of Hire eligibility
    • Above average employer paid premium coverage
  • 12 weeks Helix Paid Parental Leave option
  • 401(k) with employer matching of up to 3% and 100% Vesting on the Date of Hire
  • Comprehensive Well-Being Benefits
  • 4 weeks PTO a year

What To Expect During Your First 90 days:
  • First 30 days: you’ll spend time learning the Helix way, completing training and onboarding for your roles, and getting introduced to your team and relevant stakeholders. You’ll also gain a deeper understanding of our customers, our products, the impact we make in the lives of our communities, and how to thrive at Helix through participation in Helix U.
  • Day 30 - 60: you’ll spend time contributing to projects, deeply familiarizing yourself with team and company processes, and developing a deeper understanding of Helix’s products, services and capabilities.
  • Day 60 - 90: you’ll build your OKRs with your manager, start to take ownership of projects and initiatives on your team, and begin to demonstrate your impact on the Helix mission.

Experience in assigned program area and completion of required training programs or equivalent combination of training and experience which provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities. Possession of a BSW or MSW degree and a Commonwealth of Virginia Social Worker license are desirable.

Must Have:

    • Be part of an agile, self-directed, multi-disciplinary team that includes managers, senior solution designers, software developers and IT professionals with business expertise.
    • Provide technical expertise to deliver advanced and complex digital solutions in all phases of SDLC, including design, implementation, testing, and maintenance in multi-platform environments.
    • Develop interactive dashboards, reports, and data visualizations allowing clients to explore data and discover business insights independently.
    • Constantly and passionately learn emerging technologies, best practices, toolsets, and others to deliver state-of-the art digital solutions.
    • Provide and deliver technical solutions within large-scale ERP systems (Oracle Peoplesoft), supporting business process automation which achieves service delivery excellence and drives efficiencies.

    • Peoplesoft HCM Knowledge and Integration: Knowledge of PeopleSoft HCM operating systems, delivered application functionality, configurations and packaged application integration, focus on modules Absence Management, Time & labour as well as Benefit and payroll; Knowledge of PeopleSoft security, workflow, and tools such as PeopleSoft Update Manager (PUM), Change Assistant, and Data Mover.

Nice to have:

  • Previous OPS/Public sector exp

Description

  • The Workforce Information Network (WIN) system is a business-critical Ontario Public Service (OPS) system that is based on the Oracle PeopleSoft Human Capital Management (HCM) Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) application.
  • WIN is used to maintain OPS employees' human resources (HR), payroll, benefit, absence management, and compensation information.
  • It is operating on PeopleSoft HCM 9.2 (Image 48) on PeopleTools 8.61.09 (as of July 2026).
  • The WIN system administers compensation for approximately 68,000 OPS employees, processes payroll and enables the appropriate deductions and remittances to third parties (e.g., income tax to the Canada Revenue Agency).
  • It is the repository of employee and position data, job descriptions, and grievances/dispute data for within the OPS. The WIN system also maintains socio-demographic data voluntarily provided by OPS employees.
  • The WIN Digital Onboarding Project will enhance the WIN system in various ways. The project will:
  • Digitize critical human resources and payroll processes that are currently manual or paper-based, including onboarding, benefits enrolment, and life events management.
  • Enhance the WIN system by expanding additional employee and manager self-service capabilities (e.g., extension/end to probationary period, certificate numbers, badge numbers), enabling pay and benefits staff to focus on administrative efficiencies realized through this implementation and redirect their efforts towards more value-added activities.
  • Transition Classic+ pages to the Fluid interface by upgrading additional legacy administrative pages and implementing technical upgrades to be in sync with vendor-supported application capabilities.

title: Co-Op, Supply Chain & Logistics
description:
The Role
This is a winter / spring co-op opportunity in Norwood, MA from January 18, 2027 – June 25, 2027. Applicants must be available for the entire duration of the co-op. Start date will be January 18, 2027.


The Global Supply Chain and Logistics organization at Moderna is looking for a co-op to support work across Global Supply Planning, Master Data Management, Logistics Engineering, and Global Logistics. You will contribute to cross-functional projects that help improve supply reliability, data quality, operational execution, logistics processes, and the movement of materials across Moderna's network. This opportunity provides broad exposure to supply chain processes, systems, data, engineering, and continuous improvement, with specific assignments based on business needs and team priorities.


This position is site-based, requiring you to be at Moderna’s site full-time. This position is not eligible for remote work.


Here’s What You’ll Do

  • Support projects across Global Supply Planning, Master Data Management, Logistics Engineering, and Global Logistics.
  • Collect, organize, and analyze supply chain, inventory, master data, logistics, and process information to support business decisions.
  • Assist with maintaining accurate data, trackers, reports, and documentation used to support planning and operational activities.
  • Help develop process maps, standard work, business requirements, logistics solutions, and other materials that improve clarity, consistency, and operational performance across teams.
  • Monitor key metrics and identify trends, risks, gaps, or opportunities for improvement.
  • Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to support supply planning, material flow, transportation, warehousing, logistics engineering, and data-related initiatives.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement and digital initiatives that reduce manual work, strengthen controls, and improve visibility.
  • Support project coordination, testing, issue tracking, and follow-up activities for process or system changes.
  • Prepare analyses, summaries, and presentations, and communicate findings and recommended next steps to project teams.
  • Additional duties as may be assigned from time to time.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Basic Qualifications)

  • Current student enrolled in a Bachelors or Masters program in Supply Chain Management, Business, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Data Analytics, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Experience using Microsoft Excel to organize, analyze, and present data through coursework, employment, or project work.
  • Experience completing team-based projects and communicating results through written summaries or presentations.
  • At Moderna, we are focused on delivering on our mission by enabling talent to thrive. For this role, we are currently unable to offer immigration sponsorship. Candidates must already hold work authorization in US and be able to maintain that status without the need for future sponsorship.

Here’s What You’ll Bring to the Table (Preferred Qualifications)

  • GPA of 3.5 on a 4 scale or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated ability to work both independently as well as the ability to contribute to high performing teams.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • A desire to make an impact as part of a high-growth, transformational company that is Bold, Relentless, Curious, and Collaborative.

Our Working Model
As we build our company, we have always believed that an in-person culture is critical to our success. This role is 100% onsite, reflecting the importance of being physically present to support the work, collaborate closely with colleagues, and contribute to our site-based operations.


Working onsite enables real-time collaboration, strong team connections, direct mentorship, and the hands-on partnership needed to deliver our mission. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.


Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.

Pay & Benefits

At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work. That’s why our co-op benefits are designed to support you during your time with us —at work, at home, and everywhere in between.

title: Sr. Specialist, Quality Control, Reference Material
description:
The Role:

Moderna is seeking a highly motivated Quality Control Reference Material Sr. Specialist to join our Quality Control team. This role will contribute to the lifecycle management of reference materials, assay controls, and critical reagents supporting clinical and commercial programs. The individual will be responsible for analytical data compilation, data assessment and trending, preparation of supporting data reference documents, authoring of GMP qualification and requalification protocols and reports. The individual will coordinate and execute activities related to qualification and requalification while providing technical support and ensuring activities are performed in accordance with applicable cGMP requirements and established procedures.

Here’s What You’ll Do:

  • Execute and contribute to the creation, qualification, and requalification of reference materials, assay controls, and critical reagents.
  • Compile, review, and assess analytical data supporting reference material qualification and requalification activities, including statistical analysis, data trending, graphical evaluations, and preparation of technical data summaries using Excel, JMP, or other applicable tools.
  • Track material lifecycle milestones and timelines and communicate potential risks or impacts to relevant stakeholders.
  • Coordinate and execute activities related to the sourcing, preparation, and distribution of materials used for analytical method qualification, validation, and transfer across internal and external laboratories.
  • Coordinate activities to maintain continuity of supply for Moderna-specific materials used by internal and external laboratories.
  • Coordinate with QC laboratories, technical SMEs, and Quality stakeholders to obtain supporting analytical data, address documentation review comments, and facilitate timely completion of GMP documentation deliverables
  • Author, revise and review protocols, reports, certificates, regulatory submission content, and other relevant technical and GMP documentation.
  • Perform activities in accordance with applicable cGMP requirements, internal procedures, and quality standards.
  • Provide technical support for troubleshooting and remediation activities related to reference materials, reagents, and standards, including GMP investigations.
  • Support the retrieval, compilation, and organization of reference material qualification/requalification documentation and supporting analytical data for internal and external audits, as needed.
  • Participate in regulatory and health authority inspection preparation and on-site inspection activities.

Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)

  • Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s Degree in Chemical/Biomedical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Biochemistry, or a related discipline.
  • Experience: Minimum of 5 years (Bachelor’s) or 3 years (Master’s) of industry experience in biopharmaceutical development.
  • Specific Certifications or Training: None
  • Other Quantifiable Preference:
  • Working knowledge of relevant and current FDA, EU, ICH guidelines and regulations
  • Previous experience supporting reference standards, critical reagents, and assay controls is preferred.

title: Assistant Vice President - Central Approvals Team
description:
Some careers have more impact than others.

If you’re looking for a career where you can make a real impression, join HSBC and discover how valued you’ll be.

HSBC is one of the largest banking and financial services organizations in the world, with operations in 64 countries and territories. We aim to be where the growth is, enabling businesses to thrive and economies to prosper, and, ultimately, helping people to fulfil their hopes and realize their ambitions.

We are currently seeking an experienced professional to join our team in the role of Assistant Vice President - Central Approvals Team

Purpose of the role

The Central Approvals Team is a first line of defence global subject matter expert team responsible for managing the review and approval of financial promotions across HSBC Asset Management entities. The Central Approvals Team ensures that all marketing materials shared with clients and distribution partners meet the relevant regulatory requirements and comply with the Global Compliance Standards prescribed by HSBC. The team oversees the full process, from compliance review through approval, record-keeping and ongoing monitoring of financial promotion content across all markets and teams. It also aims to enable quicker and more efficient go-to-market for financial promotion content, supporting growth in sales engagement opportunities while ensuring adherence to all local regulatory requirements. This role sits within HSBC Asset Management Client Business, Centre of Excellence, and works closely with all other functions involved in the financial promotions management cycle to mitigate regulatory and operational risk.

As a senior member of the Central Approvals Team, a key responsibility is to support and deliver the objectives of the team. To succeed in this role, you will act as a subject matter expert and take responsibility for managing and leading country-specific operations within the scope of the Central Approvals Team. You will specialise in the regulatory requirements relating to financial promotion content and demonstrate strong risk management capability. You will also bring excellent influencing and stakeholder management skills, along with a strong understanding of business-to-business and business-to-business-to-consumer models, to operate effectively across a global stakeholder base.

In this role, you will be:

  • Manage the end-to-end compliance review and approval of all financial promotion content across HSBC Asset Management throughout the full content life cycle, coordinating self-compliance and Regulatory Compliance approvals at the point of manufacture, point of distribution and point of customisation.
  • Review all financial promotion and marketing materials produced across the business to ensure content is clear, accurate, compliant with applicable regulations, aligned to internal policies and Global Compliance Standards, and consistent with Treating Customers Fairly principles and HSBC Asset Management’s Treating Customers Fairly philosophy.
  • Apply appropriate disclaimers and disclosures to all approved materials and maintain (with Regulatory Compliance agreement) a complete disclaimer and disclosure library for all markets and investment strategies, keeping it current for regulatory and policy changes.
  • Maintain (with Regulatory Compliance agreement) the Global Compliance Checklist and ensure relevant standards, policies and procedures are developed, implemented, meet regulatory needs and are clearly understood, providing clear, accurate and timely guidance to stakeholders.
  • Publish and maintain approved documents in global and local content repositories, including Seismic, ensuring robust record-keeping, auditability and effective version control across markets and teams.
  • Manage ongoing compliance training and testing for content owners, marketing, client business and customisation teams (with Regulatory Compliance agreement), updating training and testing, the Global Compliance Checklist, and the disclaimer and disclosure library to reflect changes and ensure adoption.
  • Conduct regular oversight and monitoring of financial promotions, including quarterly quality checks through sample document reviews, producing timely management information for governance meetings, identifying improvements, and embedding lessons learned to strengthen the control environment.
  • Deliver strong risk and control management by adhering to risk, compliance, global standards and financial crime compliance requirements; preventing avoidable operational losses; avoiding or mitigating regulatory censure; ensuring no high-risk or repeat audit points; logging material breaches within required timescales with timely updates; applying the risk acceptance process where appropriate in line with data integrity management requirements; escalating control and reputational issues promptly; addressing audit and regulator issues in a timely manner; fostering a strong compliance culture; ensuring required training completion; optimising relations with regulators; and collaborating across functions including the Bangalore global service centre to support client-centric outcomes for institutional and wholesale clients.

To be successful you will be:

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, business, law or a related field and Experience working with Regulatory Compliance professionals and responding to inquiries or requests for information.
  • Strong experience in asset management compliance, with a focus on financial promotion content and Strong attention to detail and ability to analyze complex information.
  • Understanding of regulatory requirements for financial promotions in the asset management industry
  • Ability to interpret and apply the regulatory requirements w.r.t the financial promotion content.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively with different teams and stakeholders
  • Ability to work independently and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment

  • Lead pre-contract technical design, including main plant, auxiliary systems, switchgear, transformers, reactive power equipment, specifications and feasibility layouts.
  • Act as the key technical interface with EPC contractors and OEM partners, ensuring high-quality and standardised design deliverables.
  • Provide technical leadership and support to Project Development and Project Delivery teams throughout the design, construction and operation of transmission substations.
  • Lead and support engineers undertaking technical assurance of EPC design submissions, ensuring alignment with SPT standards, policies and operational requirements.
  • Lead engineering reviews, governance, assurance and approval of design calculations, models, reports and regulatory submissions.
  • Engage with EPC contractors early in the design process to improve constructability and reduce delivery risk.
  • Manage engineering interfaces with Asset Management, Engineering Standards, Network Planning and other technical teams.
  • Collaborate with Principal Engineers, Section Heads and industry specialists to share expertise and resolve complex engineering challenges.
  • Lead technical innovation across Strategic Projects, including BIM, new engineering tools, systems and contractor-led solutions.
  • Represent SPT Strategic Projects on technical matters with senior industry, regulatory and external stakeholders.
  • Develop and champion advanced engineering solutions that support the accelerated delivery of Strategic Projects.

What you’ll bring

  • Expert knowledge and proven experience in the design of 33kV to 400kV substations and associated plant.
  • Strong understanding of transmission network health, safety, technical and compliance requirements.
  • Proven experience delivering engineering outputs within a complex, fast-paced project environment.
  • Strong technical leadership skills, with experience managing or supporting engineering teams.
  • Experience working across internal teams, EPC contractors, OEMs and other external stakeholders.
  • Ability to make sound engineering decisions where information may be incomplete or requirements are evolving.
  • Strong communication, influencing and presentation skills, with the ability to use engineering analysis to support senior-level decisions.
  • A collaborative approach with the ability to drive technical improvement and transformational change.

As a minimum, you will demonstrate:


  • Degree-level engineering qualification (BSc/BEng) and/or relevant postgraduate qualification (MEng/MSc) or equivalent relevant experience. Chartered Engineer status is preferred.
  • Experience working within an engineering/EPC environment, supporting multiple large-scale strategic projects.
  • Minimum 10 years’ experience in electrical transmission substation design, including at least 5 years in a leadership role.
  • Demonstrable experience of transmission substation and plant engineering.
  • Excellent leadership, communication and stakeholder-management skills.

What’s in it for you


As well as a competitive salary which is reviewed annually, you can also enjoy a number of other benefits. With our pension scheme, we’ll double match your contribution up to a company contribution of 10%.


At ScottishPower, we believe it’s the little things we do in life that make a big difference. From helping you look after your family’s wellbeing, save for your future and take personal steps for climate action – our benefits are designed to help you do just that - so that you have everything you need to take care of your world – today and tomorrow. That’s why our benefits include:


  • 36 days annual leave
  • Holiday purchase – perfect your work/life balance with extra annual leave
  • Share Incentive Plan and Sharesave Scheme
  • Payroll giving and charity matched funding
  • Technology Vouchers – save more and spread the cost of your technology purposes
  • Count us in – pledge to reduce carbon emissions and help fight climate change
  • Electric Vehicle Schemes – to help you transition to green/clean driving
  • Cycle to Work scheme and public transport season ticket loans
  • Options to purchase dental insurance, private medical insurance, health cash plan and annual health assessments
  • Life Assurance (4x salary)
  • Access to Savesmart financial wellbeing support
  • Plus shopping, leisure, restaurant and gym discounts, and unique employee deals on travel insurance and more

Why SP Energy Networks


SP Energy Networks is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world’s largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. We keep electricity flowing to homes and businesses through Central and Southern Scotland, North Wales and in the North West of England. We operate over 4000km of cables and lines that make-up the transmission network – connecting infrastructure like wind farms into the electricity system. It’s a role that puts us right at the heart of Scotland’s ambition to be Net Zero by 2044. And we’re taking it very seriously. We’re investing >£5.5 billion into our transmission network, directly supporting the rapid growth needed in renewable energy. With diverse opportunities across our businesses and a commitment to invest in our own internal talent, ScottishPower can offer people real career opportunities that meet personal and professional goals, in a global organisation.


Inclusion, diversity, and a social purpose are at the heart of everything we do. Together with our values, they bring us together into a stronger, more sustainable business with direct links to the communities we serve. It takes all kinds of people to build a large-scale business like ours, so whatever your background, you’ll fit right in.

Job Description

About Teledyne FLIR Defense

Join Teledyne FLIR Defense, where we're dedicated to supporting critical missions with an exciting range of cutting-edge technologies. Our products include advanced surveillance sensors, unmanned air and ground vehicles, sensing devices used to detect chemicals, biological agents, radiation and explosives, and a host of other solutions that help warfighters, first responders, and search-and-rescue teams do their jobs better.

We're looking for passionate innovators eager to shape the future of the Defense and Public Safety industries. If you’re mission-driven to globally collaborate on solutions that can change the battlefield and save lives, we invite you to explore our current opportunities.

#AnyThreatAnywhere


Job Summary:


Teledyne FLIR is searching for a Theoretical Physicist with a nuclear physics background to perform the functions necessary for developing new analysis methods and algorithms for the purpose of radionuclide identification in a nuclear security and safeguards scenario as well as enhancing and improving existing methodology in the existing legacy products. Additionally, the theoretical physicist will be responsible for working with our intellectual property team to assure that all intellectual property generated is properly protected.

Primary Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Maintain current radionuclide identification algorithm/software.
  • Continually improve nuclide identification with emphasis on shielding and masking scenarios.
  • Research and development of new radioactive nuclide identification algorithms.
  • Develop and validate physics-based models for radiation transport, source characterization, and detector response.
  • Design simulation frameworks to support next-generation radiation detection systems.
  • Perform uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analysis on detection algorithms.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams to transition research concepts into deployable products.
  • Support product roadmap development through technical assessments of emerging technologies.
  • Participate in verification, validation, and performance testing of new algorithms and detector systems.
  • Generate invention disclosures and support patent application development.
  • Perform technical assessments of competitive technologies and prior art.
  • Contribute to the company's long-term intellectual property strategy.
  • Generate topical papers for select conferences (IEEE, SORMA, etc).

Job Qualifications:

  • PhD in theoretical physics, or related field.
  • Familiar with data analysis, data modeling, and Monte Carlo simulations.
  • Prior experience supporting DoD, DHS, DOE, NNSA, IAEA, or other nuclear security organizations is a plus.
  • Experience developing software in Python, C++, C, or MATLAB.
  • Experience with Geant4, GADRAS, or MCNP is a plus.
  • Working knowledge of Machine Learning.
  • Record of peer reviewed publications, patents, or technical conference presentations.
  • Experience with isotope identification performance evaluation and test methodologies.
  • Understanding of nuclear safeguards, nonproliferation, homeland security, or defense applications.
  • Hands on laboratory experience incorporating radiation detectors, sources, and data acquisition systems is required.
  • Strong verbal, written and visual communication skills.
  • A team attitude is required.
  • Ability to work responsibly and independently under minimal supervision.
  • Travel maybe required to visit tradeshows, training events, and conferences.

description:

Aspect House, Glasgow (hybrid)

Salary from £60,000 + up to 15% bonus, single cover private medical & other excellent benefits

Full-time, permanent position (happy to talk flexible working)

Help us create a better future, quicker!

Our Customer Business provides energy to millions of households and businesses across the UK. At ScottishPower we want to do the right thing for our customers. We believe in fair pricing and offer a choice of tariffs to suit customer needs. We offer products that help our customers control and protect the energy in their homes and the flexibility to help customers manage their energy accounts today, tomorrow and in the future.


This role sits within our Customer Business Complaints Team. The Senior Project Manager will bring together all the people involved in improvement projects and drive them through to successful implementation, leading the way, motivating colleagues, and helping to remove blockers in the journey.

ScottishPower is part of the Iberdrola Group, one of the world’s largest integrated utility companies and a world leader in wind energy. With a commitment to generate all of our energy from renewable resources and a drive to create the energy infrastructure of the future, we’re at the forefront of the journey to Net Zero and investing over £6m every working day to make this happen. title: Materials Planner
description:
For over 140 years our products have helped ensure the safe, reliable operations of key industries. With a passion for precision and partnership, Celeros Flow Technology continues this heritage of high performance and dependability, providing mission critical, sustainable flow control solutions for our customers around the globe.

Celeros Flow Technology is looking for individuals with a voice and a vision. We embrace change, diversity and promote new ways of looking at old ideas. We seek talented professionals to join our world-class team of innovators in a global, collaborative & multi-cultural environment, where you will be challenged, supported, and inspired to be extraordinary.

GENERAL SUMMARY

The Materials Planner will be responsible for planning and managing materials for a speciﬁc part families. This role is crucialfor ensuring that materials are available when needed to support producton schedules and ensuring producton order

completon is aligned to the schedule while maintaining optmal inventory levels by liaising with engineering, procurement,

manufacturing engineering and producton schedulers.

PRINCIPAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS)

  • Develop and maintain material requirements plans (MRP) for assigned producton cells, ensuring alignment with project schedules and customer demands.

  • Monitor inventory levels, identfying potental shortages or excesses, and recommend actons to optmise stock levels.

title: Sr Workday HRIS Analyst (Compensation)
description:
Title: Sr Workday HRIS Analyst (Compensation)

Location: Statewide Multi Use, ID
